GTA 6: Where to Find a Fighter Jet

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s not just wheeled vehicles that you can steal in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that there is only one place in the entirety of the map where you can find fighter jets, and it’s, surprisingly, very early on.
  • While the game will be pointing you more north, with Lucia being held in Hamlet and Vice City even further north, most people wouldn’t even consider looking south.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s not just wheeled vehicles that you can steal in Grand Theft Auto 6. Just as in previous games, you’ll be able to take control of some flying vehicles, be it fighter jets, personal planes or commercial planes. In this case, we’re talking about the former. These aren’t exactly useful in most scenarios, but just having one is something to be proud of, not to mention you can do some serious unnecessary damage with its missiles. This guide will help you track one down and steal it.

Recent findings suggest that there is only one place in the entirety of the map where you can find fighter jets, and it’s, surprisingly, very early on. When you start the story of Grand Theft Auto 6, you will be on the outskirts of Vice City. The small Key Lento, where small drug trafficking happens and everyone is either horny or incredibly violent. Regardless, there is an opportunity here.

While the game will be pointing you more north, with Lucia being held in Hamlet and Vice City even further north, most people wouldn’t even consider looking south. Well, if you do, you will be treated to a long road that heads into a small town called Southwind, and next to it, is the Mile Zero Air Station.

This is essentially the military base of Grand Theft Auto 6. While there are restricted areas elsewhere, this is definitely the most heavily guarded location you will encounter, and because of that, you will find some heavy firepower here.

There will be Air Force One planes, armored vehicles, tanks and, of course, fighter jets. Inside the Miel Zero Air Station sits a good number of fighter jets for stealth, but getting one isn’t exactly the easiest of tasks.

According to recent reports, in order to get to Mile Zero Air Station, you can take a couple of paths. It’s very difficult to remain undetected, almost impossible really, but if you’re able to avoid detection, you’ll be able to grab a jet. Unfortunately, when you get airborne, you’ll immediately be on their radar, in which they will send fighter jets to intercept you, which will go poorly very promptly.

There are a couple ways to get in. The first is through the main entrance near Southwind. This is heavily guarded, so if you’re doing this approach, sneak into the armored vehicle that’s generally parked next to the entrance and then drive in.

If you want to go the stealth approach, come in from the sea. The port off the western part of Mile Zero Air Station is still guarded, but there are no fences, so there’s a lot more room to move around.

It has been revealed that it’s not impossible to outrun the 5-star Wanted level when getting a fighter jet, but it’s hard. In our best attempt, we flew back into downtown. The fighter jets and choppers still chased us and damaged the jet beyond repair. What we did was, while Downtown, or in Tequesta (south of Downtown), go as high as possible.

The jets will follow, and as soon as you begin to level off, jump out. I hope you have a parachute as you’re going to fall down as far as possible until you’re level with some of the skyscrapers. Tequesta is full of helipads with at least two of them having helicopters on them.

Try to parachute over to them and land. It can be tricky, but it can be done. While the jets are still distracted high in the sky, you should be able to fly the helicopter out of the wanted zone.

Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the upcoming mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games.
  • According to recent reports, "Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods presently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making.
  • Recent findings suggest that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the newly introduced "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

According to recent reports, "Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods presently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an glitch related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon.".

Recent findings suggest that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the newly introduced "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is key for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the concern for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected.".

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the Newly introduced Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

It has been revealed that personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this upgrade does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

#51950. Tech Report: Scientists create a remarkable newly introduced rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

Tech Report: Scientists create a remarkable newly introduced rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scientists have found an unexpected fresh use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health.
  • Recent findings suggest that vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products.
  • Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists have found an unexpected fresh use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health. Researchers at the University of Córdoba have incorporated the vitamin into a rechargeable battery, demonstrating for the first time that it can serve as a catalyst in this type of energy storage system.

Recent findings suggest that vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products. The vitamin is produced by certain bacteria, which occur in nature and are also grown commercially to supply the food and pharmaceutical industries. In addition to its established applications in medicine, nutrition, and veterinary care, B12 is used to address certain nutritional deficiencies. It has also become popular alongside other B vitamins as a hangover remedy because of its potential to help reduce fatigue.

Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application. By using the vitamin to support the chemical reactions inside a battery, they have developed a prototype capable of completing up to 250 charging and discharging cycles.

How Vitamin B12 Makes a Rechargeable Battery Possible.

The new battery was developed by the Physical Chemistry research group (FQM-204) at the University of Córdoba's Chemical Institute for Energy and the Environment (IQUEMA). It uses zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air to produce electricity, with vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, playing a crucial role in the process.

To make the design work, the researchers attached vitamin B12 molecules to single-walled carbon nanotubes. The vitamin contains cobalt (III) at its center, which helps drive the electrochemical reactions needed for the battery to function.

According to recent reports, the team has previously experimented with natural molecules as battery catalysts, including hemoglobin and catalase. These substances contain iron (II) and iron (III), respectively. Vitamin B12 represents the group's third effort to use a biological molecule for this purpose, but it has delivered an key advance: a battery that can be recharged repeatedly, completing as many as 250 cycles.

Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest obstacles was keeping vitamin B12 inside the battery. Because the vitamin dissolves readily in water, it would normally be difficult to retain in a system that relies on a water-based electrolyte.

The researchers overcame this problem by securing the vitamin to carbon nanotubes, using an approach inspired by how amino acids connect to form proteins.

Manuel Cano Luna, one of the study's authors, explained that "we looked at the properties we can find in naturally occurring materials to use them in fresh batteries," while describing the team's search for useful biological compounds.

Their attachment technique imitates "the process by which amino acids bind together in proteins.".

Alongside Cano Luna, the research team included Valentín García Caballero, Miguel López León, Pablo Gómez Argudo, Luis Camacho Delgado, José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado, María Teresa Martín Romero, José Abad López, and Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero.

A Safer, Lighter Alternative to Lithium-Ion Batteries.

The findings, published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, could contribute to the development of battery technologies that depend less on the materials used in conventional lithium-ion batteries.

Although lithium-ion batteries are widely used, obtaining their raw materials can involve significant economic, environmental, and social challenges. Zinc-air batteries offer a potential alternative because they can store substantial amounts of energy relative to their weight while relying on materials that are more readily available.

Zinc is abundant and recyclable, and these batteries use oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere as part of their energy-producing reactions. Because they draw oxygen from the air rather than storing all the necessary reactants internally, they can also be lighter than other battery designs.

It has been revealed that this advantage has helped make zinc-air batteries increasingly useful in compact electronic devices, particularly hearing aids. Another benefit is their use of non-flammable, water-based electrolytes, which can reduce fire risks and improve safety.

Why Vitamin B12 Is Key to Recharging.

A major challenge in developing rechargeable zinc-air batteries is finding a catalyst that can efficiently support the chemical reactions involved in both producing and storing electricity.

According to recent reports, during discharge, the battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Recharging requires the relevant chemical reactions to proceed in the opposite direction. A suitable catalyst must therefore be effective in both processes.

According to researcher Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, vitamin B12 "has proven to meet the necessary conditions to act as a good catalyst because, during discharge, it catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water and, during recharging, it promotes the production of oxygen.".

This ability to support both reactions is what makes the vitamin particularly promising for rechargeable zinc-air battery technology.

Could Vitamin B12 Help Store Renewable Energy?

The successful prototype offers a new direction for researchers seeking affordable, sustainable alternatives to existing energy storage technologies.

If the approach can be developed further, batteries using vitamin B12 catalysts could eventually help address one of the biggest challenges facing renewable energy: storing excess electricity generated by sources such as solar and wind power for use when production falls.

In a recent development, although the technology remains at the research stage, demonstrating up to 250 charge and discharge cycles indicates that a familiar biological molecule can play an unexpected role in rechargeable battery design. The discovery adds to growing efforts to use naturally occurring substances to create safer, lighter, and more sustainable ways to store energy.

Industry News: Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big latest world headlining Version 4.0.

According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

In a recent development, the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

Recent findings suggest that the Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Sources indicate that version 4.0 introduces two fresh 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

It has been revealed that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

It has been revealed that the other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

It has been revealed that she also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Sources indicate that version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

Recent findings suggest that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be unveiled at a later date.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros.
  • Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio.
  • In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business.

According to recent reports, A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

Latest Update: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life.
  • It has been revealed that most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time.
  • It has been revealed that among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life. The discovery, made by researchers at the University of British Columbia (UBC), could help doctors identify families with a heightened genetic risk and detect cancer before it spreads.

It has been revealed that most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time. However, approximately 5% to 10% are associated with inherited mutations that can be passed from parents to their children, creating a cancer risk that may extend across generations.

It has been revealed that among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. These inherited changes can substantially raise the likelihood of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers. Testing for BRCA mutations has reshaped cancer prevention and treatment by allowing people with elevated risks to receive earlier screening and preventive care.

Now, a study published in Cancer Discovery points to another gene, CDK12, as a potentially notable marker of inherited prostate cancer risk. After examining genetic information from more than 4,500 people with aggressive prostate cancer, the researchers discovered five unrelated men with inherited mutations in CDK12. Every one of these men developed metastatic prostate cancer between ages 44 and 62, meaning the cancer had spread beyond the prostate.

Recent findings suggest that "What's striking is that every patient we identified with this inherited mutation had already developed metastatic disease by the time they were diagnosed," remarked senior author Dr. Alexander Wyatt, associate professor of urologic sciences in the UBC faculty of medicine and UBC President's Excellence Chair in Precision Oncology. "The opportunity now is to identify these families earlier and give people the chance to benefit from enhanced screening, when there are still curative treatment options.".

A Hidden Genetic Cause of Aggressive Prostate Cancer.

The discovery challenges a longstanding assumption about CDK12. Scientists previously believed that harmful changes in this gene developed spontaneously inside cancer cells rather than being inherited from a parent.

Sources indicate that to investigate whether the inherited mutations were actually contributing to the disease, the team examined the patients' tumors for a distinctive pattern of genetic damage associated with loss of CDK12 function. This molecular fingerprint helped connect the inherited mutations to the development of their cancers.

According to recent reports, "The tumors provided us with a genetic signature that pointed directly back to CDK12," mentioned lead author Dr. Sofie Tolmeijer, a postdoctoral fellow in the Wyatt lab. "It gave us compelling evidence that these inherited mutations were playing a direct role in causing their cancer.".

The findings emerged from a broad international research effort involving UBC, BC Cancer, the Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute, and the University of Washington, along with scientists at institutions in Australia, the Netherlands, Spain, and Belgium.

Sources indicate that despite the potentially serious consequences, inherited CDK12 mutations appear to be exceptionally uncommon. The researchers found them in approximately one out of every 1,000 people with aggressive prostate cancer. Even at that low frequency, they estimate that hundreds of families around the world could be affected.

Sources indicate that "While this mutation is extremely rare, the discovery could be lifesaving for the families who carry it," mentioned Dr. Tolmeijer. "Finding one person with an inherited mutation gives us the opportunity to identify other family members at risk and help them take action before cancer develops or spreads.".

Genetic Testing Could Help Detect Prostate Cancer Earlier.

One of the most promising implications of the discovery is that doctors may not need to develop entirely new testing technology to put the findings into practice.

It has been revealed that the researchers recommend including CDK12 in standard genetic testing panels used to assess hereditary prostate cancer risk. These panels examine multiple genes associated with inherited cancer susceptibility, helping identify individuals who may benefit from closer medical monitoring.

In a recent development, importantly, the clinical technology required to detect CDK12 mutations already exists. That could make expanding genetic testing relatively straightforward, potentially reducing the time and expense needed to bring the discovery into routine patient care.

"One of the most exciting aspects of this discovery is that we already have the technology needed to act on it," remarked Dr. Wyatt, who is also a senior research scientist at the Vancouver Prostate Centre and senior scientist at BC Cancer. "Adding CDK12 to existing genetic tests is relatively straightforward, which means this discovery could move from the research lab into clinical care much more promptly.".

Could the Same Mutation Increase Ovarian Cancer Risk?

The study also uncovered clues suggesting that inherited CDK12 mutations might be associated with ovarian cancer, although more research is needed to establish whether they increase the risk.

Industry observers note that several of the men with inherited CDK12 mutations had relatives with a history of ovarian cancer. The investigators also identified another person who had ovarian cancer and carried an inherited CDK12 mutation. Analysis of that person's tumor revealed the same characteristic genetic signature seen in the prostate cancer cases.

Together, these observations suggest that CDK12 could potentially play a role in hereditary cancer risk beyond the prostate. Further studies will be needed to determine how strongly the mutations are associated with ovarian cancer and whether they should influence screening recommendations.

It has been revealed that for families carrying these rare mutations, the potential benefits of identifying their genetic risk could be substantial. Earlier testing may give relatives the opportunity to receive closer surveillance and, if cancer develops, begin treatment before it reaches an advanced stage.

"With the right genetic testing and screening programs, we envision a future where no one who inherits one of these mutations dies from cancer," noted Dr. Wyatt.

According to recent reports, the research received funding from the Prostate Cancer Foundation, Terry Fox Research Institute, Canadian Cancer Society, Canadian Institutes of Health Research, Michael Smith Health Research BC, U.S. National Institutes of Health, BC Cancer Foundation, and other funding partners.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck.
  • According to recent reports, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide.
  • By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

According to recent reports, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

Industry observers note that there's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that newly introduced games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

It has been revealed that as for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

#51937. NASA pushes Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1250 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

NASA pushes Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky.
  • During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart.
  • "NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," stated Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky. The faster these blades spin, the more lift they can generate, potentially allowing future aircraft to carry heavier scientific instruments and travel greater distances across the Red Planet.

During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart. The experiments took place inside a specialized chamber designed to reproduce the harsh atmospheric conditions on Mars. Results from 137 test runs could help engineers develop a newly introduced generation of more powerful aircraft capable of carrying scientific equipment.

"NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," stated Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL. "That's not an easy ask. While everything about Mars is hard, flying there is just about the hardest thing you can do. That's because its atmosphere is so incredibly thin that it is hard to generate lift, and yet Mars has significant gravity.".

Ingenuity made history on April 19, 2021, when it became the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another world. However, it was designed primarily to demonstrate that flight on Mars was possible, not to transport scientific instruments. NASA now hopes to go much further. Its recently unveiled SkyFall project, along with other potential future aircraft, could carry sensors and scientific instruments to investigate Mars from the air. Flying at low altitudes would provide valuable information to support future robotic and human missions.

Why Flying on Mars Requires Extreme Rotor Speeds.

Sources indicate that helicopters generate more thrust by spinning their rotors faster or using blades with a larger diameter. That basic principle applies on Earth and Mars, but the Red Planet presents a much greater engineering challenge.

Sources indicate that mars has an atmosphere only about 1% as dense as Earth's, leaving helicopter blades with far fewer air molecules to push against. To produce enough lift, engineers must operate rotors at exceptionally high speeds, bringing their tips close to the speed of sound. Small rotors on Earth can also spin thousands of times per minute, but the denser atmosphere makes it unnecessary to push their tips toward supersonic speeds to generate substantial lift.

It has been revealed that during Ingenuity's 72 flights on Mars, its engineers limited the helicopter's composite-skinned foam rotors to 2,700 revolutions per minute. This restriction served two crucial purposes. It kept the blades away from the complex and potentially unpredictable conditions near the sound barrier, and it provided a safety margin in case sudden winds (from a dust devil, for instance) caused the blade tips to move faster relative to the surrounding air.

It has been revealed that "If Chuck Yeager were here, he'd tell you things can get squirrely around Mach 1," said JPL's Jaakko Karras, the rotor test lead. "With that in mind, we planned Ingenuity's flights to keep the rotor blade tips at Mach 0.7 with no wind so that if we encountered a Martian headwind while in flight, the rotor tips wouldn't go supersonic. But we want more performance from our next-gen Mars aircraft. We needed to know that our rotors could go faster safely.".

The speed of sound also differs considerably between the two planets. At sea level on Earth, Mach 1 is approximately 760 mph (1,223 kph). On Mars, sound travels at roughly 540 mph (869 kph), largely because the atmosphere is much colder and consists primarily of carbon dioxide.

NASA Tests Supersonic Rotors in a Mars Simulation Chamber.

In a recent development, to determine whether the newly introduced blades could safely reach these extreme speeds, Karras and his colleagues used JPL's historic 25-Foot Space Simulator. The rotor systems were developed and manufactured by AeroVironment in Simi Valley, California.

It has been revealed that the researchers began with a three-bladed rotor designed for potential future Mars helicopters. After installing it inside the chamber, they removed the surrounding air and introduced a carefully controlled amount of carbon dioxide to recreate the thin Martian atmosphere. They then spun the rotor at progressively higher speeds while exposing it to simulated winds.

It has been revealed that because the experiment involved the possibility of a rotor breaking apart at supersonic speeds, engineers reinforced part of the chamber with sheet metal. The team monitored the experiment from a control room located just a few yards away, using instruments and a camera to track the rotor's performance.

The rotor eventually reached 3,750 revolutions per minute, bringing its blade tips to Mach 0.98, just below the speed of sound. Engineers then switched on a fan to produce headwinds against the spinning blades. With each successive test, they increased the wind speed to push the system further.

Breaking the Sound Barrier Boosts Lift by 30%.

The experiments ultimately drove the rotor tips to Mach 1.08, surpassing the sound barrier and increasing the aircraft's lift capability by 30%. Crucially, the blades survived the supersonic conditions.

Sources indicate that that additional lift could make a major difference for future missions. More powerful Mars helicopters could transport heavier scientific instruments, advanced sensors, and larger batteries, allowing them to conduct more ambitious investigations and remain airborne for longer periods.

Sources indicate that following the successful tests of the three-bladed design, the team evaluated a second rotor intended for SkyFall. This version has two blades that are slightly longer than those used in the first configuration. Because of their greater length, the blade tips could reach the same near-supersonic speed at a lower rotational rate of 3,570 revolutions per minute before simulated headwinds were introduced.

"The successful testing of these rotors was a major step toward proving the feasibility of flight in more demanding environments, which is key for next-gen vehicles," said Shannah Withrow-Maser, an aerodynamicist from NASA's Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley and member of the test team. "We thought we'd be lucky to hit Mach 1.05, and we reached Mach 1.08 on our last runs. We're still digging into the data, and there may be even more thrust on the table. These next-gen helicopters are going to be amazing.".

Next-Generation Mars Helicopters Could Launch in 2028.

Sources indicate that engineers working on SkyFall have already incorporated the fresh test results into the project's performance specifications. The findings provide an notable foundation for designing helicopters that can operate under more demanding conditions while carrying substantially more equipment than Ingenuity.

Inspired by the historic success of Ingenuity, which remains the only rotorcraft ever to fly on another planet, SkyFall is designed to transport three next-generation helicopters to Mars in December 2028.

If successfully developed and deployed, these aircraft could expand the possibilities for exploring Mars, providing scientists with a fresh way to investigate the planet's surface and gather information from locations that may be difficult for traditional rovers to reach.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that alongside Limit Zero Breakers, the upcoming RPG Astrae Oratio is arguably the biggest and most interesting launch NCSoft have in the chamber.
  • Recent findings suggest that with the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans.
  • Industry observers note that "Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that alongside Limit Zero Breakers, the upcoming RPG Astrae Oratio is arguably the biggest and most interesting launch NCSoft have in the chamber. Set in a world of magic and modernity co-existing side-by-side, it features gorgeous anime-inspired art and interesting gameplay. Or at least the latter is what the Astrae Oratio dev team will hope.

Recent findings suggest that with the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans. With combat being so different to other games on the market, Lim has been eager to demonstrate to fans that their feedback has been heard.

Industry observers note that "Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement. We are refining things so that combat can be enjoyed more smoothly by the official launch.".

However, Lim was also quick to reiterate exactly why Astrae Oratio's more interactive take on combat, contrary to a popular trend in other games towards auto-battler mechanics, was so notable.

"We wanted to capture both the tactile satisfaction of directly controlling your character and the strategic thrill of planning your next move. The starting point for combat in Astrae Oratio was combining the excitement of fighting games, things like reading your opponent’s movements, finding openings, and stringing together combos, with the resource management of turn-based games.

"What connects these is AP, the action resource. By choosing whether to invest in attacks and press the advantage or save it for responding, you find yourself thinking about both moment-to-moment inputs and your next move.

"Ultimately, we want to bring each character’s unique fighting style to life in combat and allow players to gain the advantage using their own judgment and inputs.".

Notably, although Lim does defend the original design intent behind how Astrae Oratio will work, he also went into detail on the specific pain points from players that they wanted to address.

Recent findings suggest that "The forced use of specific characters, the disappearance of remaining AP when an enemy is defeated, and the insufficient rewards for successful parries that you mentioned are also notable feedback items we identified in that process. The current rules are not set in stone.

Sources indicate that "In particular, we plan to rework how leftover AP is handled so the flow of combat isn’t interrupted, and enhance parrying so that landing a successful parry feels genuinely rewarding. We will continue making adjustments based on the feedback from the test and by validating those results moving forward.".

All of these are, of course, valid concerns for many fans. But it's clear that the folks behind Astrae Oratio have confidence in their vision for combat. And in truth I can't blame them, as nowadays it seems as though combat is considered a 'solved problem', even where there's room to experiment and tweak.

So, in that regard, it's refreshing to see NCSoft's development team look more closely at what they can do to change things. Although if you are concerned about playing all the time manually and the pressure that it invokes, Lim was quick to point out changes which will make it easier for those wanting a more laid-back experience.

In a recent development, "To preserve the advantages of manual combat, where you make your own judgments and inputs, we plan to maintain a certain degree of efficiency over auto-combat. However, to reduce the fatigue of repeated play, we are improving the pacing of auto-combat and also reviewing additional speed-up options.

It has been revealed that "We also plan to significantly expand the limits on boosted play to avoid inconveniencing players, and while it won’t be a traditional sweep mechanic, we are developing a feature that allows you to acquire needed resources more conveniently. We will strive to deliver both the thrill of hands-on combat and the convenience needed for daily grinding.".

Overall, it seems as if the closed beta was a success for Astrae Oratio, and even the developers themselves admit that it was exciting to get new feedback from players out in the wild.

According to recent reports, "The positive responses to the story and art gave us great encouragement. We also received diverse opinions on what felt fun in the combat system and what needs improvement, and based on this, we will strive to deliver an even more polished version.".

And as for how it felt for fans to get their hands on Astrae Oratio from all across the world?

According to recent reports, "There were differences in detailed reactions by region, but the way consumers appreciated the appealing content we intended to present was similar. It gave the sense that there are no borders when it comes to what you love. Indeed, you could say 'when it comes to otaku, we are the world.'" I think that Astrae Oratio is shaping up to be a particularly interesting fresh entry in NCSoft's catalogue. And while I can never truly forgive them for canning the surprisingly fun little MOBA called Battle Crush, I think that Astrae Oratio and Limit Zero Breakers make for exciting substitutes.

If you want to see what they'll be competing against when Astrae Oratio does launch, well, there's no need to trawl through our back catalogue to find out. Instead, why not dig into our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some of our choice picks?

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have revealed that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find upcoming jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies.".

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting vital leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers.".

Recent findings suggest that their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote.".

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

#51929. 8 Soulslikes With the Most Unforgiving Checkpoint Systems

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (946 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

8 Soulslikes With the Most Unforgiving Checkpoint Systems

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (946 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding the next checkpoint in any Soulslike game feels like a godsend.
  • While there are Soulslikes out there that are generally pretty generous when it comes to their checkpoint systems, there are others that are extremely punishing.
  • According to recent reports, in this list, we take a look at eight games that have a punishing checkpoint system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding the next checkpoint in any Soulslike game feels like a godsend. After fighting through waves of enemies, gathering a ton of loot and experience points, you’re hopeful that the next checkpoint will come soon so you can level up.

While there are Soulslikes out there that are generally pretty generous when it comes to their checkpoint systems, there are others that are extremely punishing. The more punishing checkpoint systems tend to feel more rewarding, but are also the cause of a lot of frustration.

According to recent reports, in this list, we take a look at eight games that have a punishing checkpoint system. Whether it's because their checkpoints are too far apart, levels feature too many enemies, or the runbacks to the bosses are miserable, you will find it in this list.

Demon’s Souls essentially started the idea of including unforgiving checkpoint systems in games. Unlike later FromSoftware games that provide plenty of shortcuts and checkpoints near challenging encounters, Demon’s Souls often forces players to replay lengthy sections of a level.

Industry observers note that the Shrine of Storms and Valley of Defilement are two clear examples of this, where the trek between checkpoints, otherwise known as Archstones, is more intimidating than the bosses themselves. Plus, the game’s unique “World Tendency” mechanic, which makes the world more challenging with each death, makes the lack of checkpoints hit even harder.

Industry observers note that lords of the Fallen’s most unique trait is its checkpoint system, which comes in the form of Vestiges. There are permanent Vestiges and Umbral Flowerbeds, temporary Vestiges that players can activate by planting a seed.

In a recent development, while the permanent Vestiges remain at all times, they are extremely far apart in each level, making it so the player has to rely on planting Vestige Seeds into Umbral Flowerbeds. However, this is easier said than done considering Vestige Seeds are generally rare.

According to recent reports, even though Hollow Knight: Silksong is primarily a Metroidvania, and an excellent one at that, it has enough Soulslike elements that make it fit right at home in the genre. And it fits right at home in this list due to its checkpoint system that can be a downright pain in the butt.

Silksong’s checkpoints are rarely near each other. This is especially punishing in a game like Silksong since dying could lead to the player having to repeat a series of platforming challenges. The lack of checkpoints is especially noticeable for some bosses, like The Last Judge and Groal the Great, each with extensive platforming runbacks to the boss arena.

Dark Souls 2’s infamous bonfires aren’t disliked because of their distance from each other, but for the excruciating number of enemies between them. Some gaps between bonfires are littered with too many elite enemies, mobs, traps, and more, making the game sometimes feel like a chore.

The checkpoints are especially punishing when it comes to the game’s bosses, since the bosses are not easy and the runbacks between bonfire and boss arena are excruciatingly long. Having to trek all the way back to the boss arena just to attempt to boss fight again is simply tiring.

It has been revealed that mortal Shell’s checkpoint system is unforgiving for multiple reasons. One, they are generally well-hidden and away from areas worth exploring, and two, Mortal Shell’s level design is filled with interconnecting paths that make it easy to get lost.

Industry observers note that usually in a Soulslike, you lose experience points or resources upon death, such as “Souls” in Dark Souls. However, in Mortal Shell, you lose both Tar and Glimpses, which are two necessary resources for character progression. Losing two important resources instead of one makes finding a checkpoint even more stress-inducing.

According to recent reports, the checkpoint system in Bleak Faith: Forsaken is punishing due to the absurdly large environments players will be exploring during a playthrough. Not only are the levels huge, but they are also genuinely confusing, causing players to easily get lost.

Industry observers note that due to the low budget and only a three-person team behind the project, it can sometimes feel like you’re playing a game with no clear direction. This, plus the fact that checkpoints are few and far between, can make it feel like you’re always being punished.

Hellpoint’s checkpoints come in the form of Breaches, and even though they are key to progression, they don’t act like your typical Soulslike checkpoint. For starters, they don’t restore your healing supplies, meaning they can’t be used as a way to survive longer. Players have to instead focus on inventory management for that.

On the other hand, Breaches are scattered throughout large levels, meaning there are tons of enemies between them. Dying in Hellpoint results in dropping Axions, an important resource for leveling, but also spawns a ghost of your past character that you have to fight when returning to the spot of death. This can make reaching the next checkpoint even more difficult than before.

Recent findings suggest that bloodborne has some notoriously distant checkpoints, especially when compared to other FromSoftware titles and Soulslikes in general. This is punishing enough, but the fact that the game is downright brutal when it comes to the amount of damage enemies deal, distant checkpoints feel even more punishing.

Industry observers note that some examples of a few lamp checkpoints include Nightmare of Mensis and Forbidden Woods, some of the hardest areas in the game that have long stretches of dangerous enemies. Players can expect to die many times in these areas alone before even coming close to the next checkpoint, depending on skill level.

Sources indicate that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, upcoming reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

In a recent development, the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Recent findings suggest that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Sources indicate that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

In a recent development, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

In a recent development, this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

In a recent development, marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

According to recent reports, although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

#51927. Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1584 w)

Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates.
  • Recent findings suggest that for years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty.
  • Sources indicate that but newly introduced research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates. As these protective barriers disappear, they expose towering walls of solid ice. Whether these cliffs remain standing or collapse could play a major role in Antarctica's future ice loss and its contribution to rising sea levels worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that for years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty. According to this theory, a cliff that grows too tall will collapse under its own weight, exposing an even taller wall of ice farther inland. That new cliff would then collapse, potentially setting off a chain reaction that causes the ice sheet to retreat rapidly.

Sources indicate that but newly introduced research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption. The findings suggest that the fate of an Antarctic ice cliff depends on much more than its height, and that even dramatic collapses do not necessarily lead to an unstoppable retreat.

Published in the journal Science, the study examined satellite observations of more than 15,000 Antarctic ice cliffs collected over four years. Researchers discovered a surprising pattern: When the cliffs collapsed, they sometimes retreated much faster than existing models predicted. Yet rather than continuing to disintegrate, the affected glaciers soon stabilized.

Industry observers note that "We found that when the cliffs were retreating, they were doing so faster than what has been modeled, which would mean more ice loss and higher contributions of sea level rise," says study author Caroline Needell, a graduate student in the MIT-WHOI Joint Program. "But because we found that the retreat was short-lived, and all the glaciers eventually stabilized, that would suggest that things won't be so bad. We don't see this runaway effect.".

The study's co-authors are Catherine Walker, an assistant scientist at WHOI, and Jeremy Bassis, an associate professor at the University of Michigan.

Why Scientists Expected Antarctica's Ice Cliffs to Collapse.

According to recent reports, the possibility of runaway ice cliff collapse is described by a theory called marine ice cliff instability (MICI). It proposes that when an exposed ice wall reaches a critical height, its own weight makes it structurally unstable. If the cliff falls and reveals an even taller wall behind it, the process could repeat, progressively eating away at the Antarctic ice sheet.

In a recent development, earlier research investigated this possibility primarily through computer models. Scientists used the physical properties of ice to estimate how enormous frozen cliffs should behave, then compared those calculations with a limited number of observations from Antarctica. These studies suggested that cliffs taller than approximately 100 meters were particularly vulnerable to collapse.

It has been revealed that "Predictive ice-sheet models that have been used so far to represent ice cliff instability just take into account cliff height," Needell notes. "That's the only variable that matters. And once the cliff height reaches the critical threshold, usually 100 meters, it should initiate this runaway effect of ice sheet retreat.".

Needell and her colleagues wanted to test those predictions against a much larger collection of real-world measurements. They sought to determine how tall Antarctica's ice cliffs actually become and whether their collapse consistently triggers the destructive chain reactions predicted by existing models.

Satellites Reveal Surprising Ice Cliff Stability.

In a recent development, to investigate, the researchers turned to NASA's Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2). This spacecraft repeatedly travels over Earth's polar regions, using a laser-based instrument called an altimeter to measure elevations with great precision. Its observations track the heights of glaciers, ice sheets, and sea ice, as well as ocean levels in and around Antarctica.

According to recent reports, the team analyzed measurements gathered between 2019 and 2023, examining more than 15,000 ice cliffs at three-month intervals. Most were far shorter than the height considered dangerous by earlier models. The average cliff stood approximately 30 meters tall, although a small number exceeded the proposed 100-meter instability threshold.

The researchers also searched for characteristics that might explain why some cliffs remained stable while others retreated.

Sources indicate that one crucial clue came from the broken ice accumulating in front of the cliffs. Known as mélange, this material consists of a slushy mixture of sea ice and fragments of icebergs. Cliffs that remained relatively stationary tended to have thicker accumulations of mélange, suggesting that the debris could help support the towering ice walls.

"We measured mélange height and found taller cliffs have thicker mélange, which could be a built-in stabilizing effect," Needell explains.

Surrounding seawater provided another possible source of stability. The observations indicated that deeper water can exert greater supporting pressure against an ice cliff, helping counteract the forces that might otherwise cause it to collapse.

Sources indicate that together, these findings suggest that the stability of Antarctica's ice cliffs cannot be predicted by height alone. Conditions in the water surrounding the ice may also determine whether a cliff remains standing.

Antarctica's Tallest Ice Cliffs Collapse, Then Stabilize.

"After we did that global analysis, we thought, ok, let's zoom in on the tallest cliffs and see how they're behaving," Needell notes.

The researchers selected four locations around Antarctica where satellites had recorded some of the tallest ice cliffs. Each stood approximately 100 meters high, with the tallest reaching 127 meters. The team then reconstructed how these cliffs changed at three-month intervals throughout the four-year study.

It has been revealed that the results initially appeared to support the idea that extremely tall cliffs are unstable. These towering walls did collapse, and the glaciers behind them retreated at speeds substantially greater than those anticipated by existing MICI models.

However, the retreat did not continue indefinitely.

"But that retreat was short-lived," Needell notes.

Instead of retreating farther inland in a continuous series of collapses, the glaciers stabilized and eventually advanced outward toward the ocean again.

Sources indicate that "It's this rapid retreat, punctuated by periods of stabilization," Needell says. "That was puzzling to us. Then, we thought: We need to look at all the things that affect cliff height.".

The unexpected pattern suggested that some overlooked physical processes were interrupting the collapse before it could develop into a sustained chain reaction.

Hidden Ridges Beneath the Ice Act as Natural Speed Bumps.

To understand what was stopping the retreat, the team examined the shape of the land beneath Antarctica's ice sheet.

According to recent reports, this underlying terrain, known as bed topography, can strongly influence the height and stability of the ice above it. When the ground is relatively flat, the visible slope of the ice more closely reflects the thickness of the ice itself. But when the terrain rises into a ridge or bump, the ice resting on that elevated ground is thinner than its overall surface elevation might suggest.

These buried rises can function like natural speed bumps. By reducing the thickness of the overlying ice, they can make exposed cliffs shorter and less vulnerable to collapse.

When the scientists compared the locations of stabilizing ice cliffs with measurements of Antarctica's underlying terrain, they found that the cliffs frequently stopped retreating where the ground rose beneath them.

Industry observers note that the researchers identified another important process. Taller cliffs tended to "thin out" more rapidly as they collapsed. Rather than remaining towering, unstable walls, they could swiftly shrink into shorter cliffs that were better able to withstand further collapse.

These effects help explain why the researchers observed rapid initial ice loss followed by periods of stability, rather than the continuous retreat anticipated by earlier models.

What the Discovery Means for Future Sea Level Rise.

The findings could help scientists improve predictions of how Antarctica's ice sheet will respond to continued warming.

Although the researchers observed some cliffs collapsing faster than expected, the rapid retreat was temporary in the locations they studied. This challenges the assumption that crossing a particular height threshold inevitably leads to runaway collapse.

According to recent reports, the results do not mean Antarctica's ice sheet is safe from further losses. Instead, they reveal that predicting its future requires accounting for several interacting factors, including the shape of the land beneath the ice, the rate at which ice becomes thinner, the depth of surrounding water, and the stabilizing effects of broken ice.

"Now we know what to look for," Needell notes. "We really need to know the bed topography, and we need to know the ice thinning rate, in order to get ice cliff instability right, because this value really matters in the context of projecting sea level rise.".

By incorporating these additional processes into ice sheet models, scientists may be able to produce more reliable estimates of Antarctica's future contribution to global sea level rise.

It has been revealed that the research received partial support from NASA, the U.S. National Science Foundation, and the DOMINOS project, which is part of the International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration.

  • We know that Season 2 is introducing a massive new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the upcoming content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a massive new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the fresh season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

According to recent reports, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

According to recent reports, audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director indicates it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

It has been revealed that A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.
