The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

It has been revealed that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the latest class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

It has been revealed that echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Industry observers note that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Recent findings suggest that reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as upcoming quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder.
  • The condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening.
  • It has been revealed that the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder. Now, researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have uncovered evidence that challenges 30 years of established thinking and could open the door to a new treatment.

The condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening. A new study published in Immunity identifies a previously underrecognized problem involving natural killer (NK) cells, immune cells that normally help the body eliminate infected cells.

It has been revealed that the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur. The discovery also points to a possible treatment using existing medications called JAK inhibitors, which could be particularly valuable for patients who do not respond to current therapies.

Sources indicate that "This study has revealed a new target for this inflammatory disorder and sets the scene for future clinical studies to explore the use of JAK inhibitors or other drugs to neutralize interferon gamma in patients with MKD," states Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author of the study. "This could lead to a targeted treatment that hasn't been tried before.".

Why a Rare Immune Disease Causes Dangerous Inflammation.

MKD is a lifelong condition known to affect hundreds of children and adults around the world, although researchers suspect that many people with the disorder have never been diagnosed. Patients experience recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and inflammation in the abdomen. The most serious episodes can cause potentially fatal complications.

In a recent development, for roughly three decades, research into the disease has largely centered on macrophages, immune cells that help coordinate the body's inflammatory defenses. Existing treatments are designed to block an inflammatory signal released by these cells. However, approximately half of patients do not respond adequately, leaving a major need for better treatment options.

To investigate what might be missing from the prevailing explanation, the Garvan team examined blood samples from people with MKD and studied preclinical models of the disorder.

Industry observers note that their experiments revealed a significant defect in natural killer cells, which play an important role in the body's early defenses against viral infections. In MKD, these cells fail to mature properly and struggle to perform one of their most important functions: destroying infected cells before an infection can spread.

The consequences go beyond an impaired ability to fight infection. When natural killer cells cannot eliminate their targets, they release large amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, activating other parts of the immune system and potentially triggering widespread inflammation.

In a recent development, "We found that these immune cells are essentially misfiring," explains Professor Rogers. "NK cells are loaded with toxic ammunition, stored in granules that are released to kill infected cells. However, in MKD these toxic granules can't be released from NK cells and remain trapped inside. When an NK cell fails to kill its target, it compensates by shouting for help, pumping out large amounts of interferon gamma - a powerful inflammatory signal. This activates other immune cells and causes the dangerous fever and widespread inflammation seen in patients.".

Discovery Challenges 30 Years of Immune Disease Research.

The findings suggest that natural killer cell dysfunction, rather than macrophage activity alone, plays a central role in driving MKD.

Dr. Marcia Munoz, Group Leader in the Rogers Lab and lead researcher on the study, states the results represent a major change in how scientists understand the disease.

"This really turns on its head 30 years of dogma about what was thought to be the underlying mechanism of disease. In MKD, the primary problem is in NK cells and not in macrophages, as previously believed," she claims.

To investigate how this cellular defect contributes to the disorder, the Garvan researchers collaborated with Professor Mariapia Degli-Esposti and scientists at Monash University.

Industry observers note that using preclinical models, the team established a connection between malfunctioning natural killer cells and the severe symptoms associated with MKD. Their experiments revealed that when the immune system cannot clear a viral infection, the resulting inflammatory response can cause extensive damage to organs.

These results help explain why a disorder involving defective immune defenses can also produce episodes of extreme inflammation.

Existing Drug Indicates Promise for a Newly introduced Treatment.

The discovery has already helped guide an experimental treatment approach for a severely affected infant.

Working with doctors at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, the researchers explored whether baricitinib could reduce the excessive inflammatory signaling associated with MKD.

According to recent reports, baricitinib belongs to a class of medications known as JAK inhibitors. These drugs interfere with signaling pathways used by the immune system, including those involved in responses to interferon gamma. The medication is already used to treat other immune-related conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema.

Doctors added baricitinib to the infant's existing treatment regimen and subsequently observed an improvement in the child's condition. Inflammatory flare-ups became less frequent, and severe inflammation affecting the gastrointestinal tract began to heal.

Although the results from a single patient cannot establish whether the treatment will work more broadly, the improvement provides encouraging early evidence for a strategy that targets a different part of the inflammatory process.

The researchers believe their findings provide a foundation for future clinical studies investigating JAK inhibitors and other medications that block interferon gamma activity in patients with MKD, particularly those who have not benefited from standard treatments.

Discovery Could Help Explain Other Genetic Diseases.

The potential implications extend beyond MKD itself.

Researchers have introduced the term 'prenylopathies' to describe a family of genetic disorders involving the same metabolic pathway affected in MKD. Early findings suggest that these related diseases may share a similar underlying problem involving natural killer cells that fail to function properly and instead generate excessive inflammatory signals.

If further studies confirm this connection, scientists may be able to identify common disease mechanisms and develop more targeted approaches to diagnosis and treatment across multiple disorders.

"Confirming this link could help end the diagnostic odyssey many patients endure for years or even decades before receiving effective treatment," claims Professor Rogers.

Professor Mike Rogers is a Conjoint Professor at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney. Dr. Marcia Munoz is a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney.

Materials provided by Garvan Institute of Medical Research. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

It has been revealed that as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco revealed in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business aims, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation.".

Sources indicate that the press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the company. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

In a recent development, bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is right now in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nioh 3 has received a hot newly introduced update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an matter that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into concerns with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Recent findings suggest that finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Industry observers note that hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar is promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 to players in mainland China, even though the game hasn't been approved for official sale there.
  • Sources indicate that according to a Reuters report published on November 18, Rockstar posted a GTA 6 preorder-related video on Douyin, the Chinese counterpart to TikTok, on November 12.
  • Industry observers note that the Douyin account is verified under Rockstar International Limited and showed a Shanghai IP location when Reuters reviewed it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rockstar is promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 to players in mainland China, even though the game hasn't been approved for official sale there. It's an unusual situation for one of the biggest debuts of the year, but the firm's social media activity makes it clear that Chinese players are still part of the audience it's trying to reach.

Sources indicate that according to a Reuters report published on November 18, Rockstar posted a GTA 6 preorder-related video on Douyin, the Chinese counterpart to TikTok, on November 12. The video encouraged customers to preload the game ahead of its worldwide November 19 release.

Industry observers note that the Douyin account is verified under Rockstar International Limited and showed a Shanghai IP location when Reuters reviewed it. By November 18, it had attracted around 480,000 followers and more than 300,000 likes. That's a sizeable audience for a game that can't be sold through officially approved channels in mainland China.

The promotion itself isn't complicated. Rockstar was telling fans that GTA 6 was available to preload on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, just as it had been doing for players elsewhere. What's unusual is the market receiving that message.

Reuters was able to access both the account and its promotional video in China. Neither Rockstar nor the National Press and Publication Administration, the country's regulator, had responded to the publication's requests for comment when the report was filed.

In a recent development, this isn't the same as Rockstar announcing an official Chinese release. A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China. The studio also hasn't mentioned that an approved release is on the way.

It has been revealed that imported video games have to pass a government approval process before they can be officially sold in mainland China. The authorities scrutinize content such as violence, sexual material, and politically sensitive themes. Given what Grand Theft Auto is about, it's not difficult to see why the series might face obstacles.

Reuters reports that the Grand Theft Auto franchise has never received official approval for sale in mainland China. GTA 6 is also missing from the regulator's published lists of approved imported games. That's the key point here. It's not a new announcement that the game has been banned outright, but rather that it lacks the approval required for an official domestic release.

A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast is particularly striking because Rockstar is treating GTA 6 as a worldwide event. The game released on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and its marketing has reached far beyond the countries where ordinary retail sales are available.

Of course, an official sales restriction doesn't necessarily stop people from playing the game. Reuters claims Chinese players have been using foreign console accounts or buying imported boxed editions that include download codes. One Douyin user who noted he was in Beijing posted about obtaining a Hong Kong edition for roughly 500 yuan, or about $75.

According to recent reports, that doesn't make those purchases part of an officially approved Chinese distribution channel. It simply shows that a market can exist for a game even when the usual local release process isn't available.

Industry observers note that it's also worth distinguishing China's situation from the ratings concerns seen in other territories. GTA 6 almost ran into trouble in South Korea, but the matter in mainland China concerns the separate approval system for imported games. They aren't interchangeable cases.

Industry observers note that for now, Rockstar can speak to a substantial Chinese audience while GTA 6 remains unavailable for officially approved domestic sales. Whether that situation changes is something only a later regulatory decision could settle. Until then, its Douyin account is a reminder that the game's reach doesn't end at the borders of its official markets.

#51913. Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (792 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and notable pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.
  • Research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions.
  • These medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and notable pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.

Research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions. This is because semaglutide acts on the brain to increase the feeling of fullness and to decrease appetite.

These medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however. Our multidisciplinary research team at the University of Alberta is working to improve obesity care for people of all ages and to understand why some people respond better to semaglutide than others, and how their weight loss can be maintained over time.

We are investigating the role of energy metabolism as a potentially important piece in a complex puzzle.

Research has shown semaglutide medications to improve quality of life, blood markers such as sugar or cholesterol, strength and overall health. Weight loss is only one measure of how well they work.

We are exploring whether people’s responses to these medications could lie in individual factors such as genetics, metabolism, body composition, lifestyle, microbiota, associated diseases, age and sex.

It has been revealed that energy metabolism may also be an key piece of this puzzle. This is a measure of the total calories consumed (in) and the total calories burned (out). We burn calories all the time: for vital processes like breathing and thinking, physical activities like going to the gym and the everyday act of digesting food.

When we lose weight, our bodies naturally need less energy. But sometimes, the body goes into an extra “energy-saving mode,” burning even fewer calories than we would expect. This is called metabolic adaptation, or adaptive thermogenesis.

Think of it like a light bulb that automatically dims to save electricity. This is one reason why losing weight can become more difficult over time, sometimes leading to a weight-loss plateau.

Changes in body weight and composition (the amount of fat and fat-free mass in our bodies) play an notable role in energy metabolism. Both fat and fat-free mass use energy, even when we are resting. As we lose these tissues, our bodies naturally burn fewer calories.

Researchers are still trying to understand whether weight-loss medications influence these processes differently. If we can understand how our bodies use energy during and after weight loss, this could help us develop better strategies for maintaining weight loss over the long term.

We published a recent review of studies investigating the effects of GLP-1 therapies on energy utilization. We found a few studies exploring how semaglutide affects resting energy use, with findings that were neutral or inconclusive.

The question of how semaglutide impacts energy use is an emerging area of study, and remains an open question for exploration.

At the University of Alberta, we have a gold-standard method to measure energy utilization called a whole-room indirect calorimeter. This is a rare research facility and is similar to a hotel suite that can precisely measure each component of energy use. This room can isolate the effects of changes in someone’s calorie burning at rest, after eating and during exercise.

Industry observers note that we are currently recruiting research participants with blood sugar regulation challenges, such as insulin resistance or diabetes, who are about to start semaglutide treatment. We will follow their weight loss journey over six months to investigate changes in body weight and composition, and energy utilization using sophisticated approaches.

Understanding how semaglutide influences energy use and body composition, and how these changes interact, could be an key step toward explaining why individuals respond differently to weight-loss treatment.

Industry observers note that this will allow us to contribute to more personalized approaches to obesity and Type 2 diabetes management in the future. Having a better understanding of how energy use changes with semaglutide-induced weight loss will also help us to better anticipate potential non-responders (people who do not lose weight) and offer alternative treatments sooner in their health journey.

Importantly, current evidence suggests that if you are taking semaglutide or considering starting treatment, you should make a few lifestyle changes.

Materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Giovanna Guimaraes Lopes Bergamasco, Andrea M. Haqq, Carla Prado, and Rachel J. Skow. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

According to recent reports, the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there's one thing The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom have taught us, it's that players will eventually find a way to turn even the simplest combat encounter into an opportunity for an unnecessarily impressive trickshot.

Apparently, that mindset isn't going anywhere, even when you take away the open-world freedom of those games, even when we are talking about a more contained gameplay like Ocarina of Time Remake.

A Japanese player recently shared an incredible clip of their own in the newest version of Ocarina of Time, taking down four ReDeads with only four carefully aimed Light Arrows!

Sources indicate that instead of shooting directly at the enemies, Adult Link fires his arrow high into the sky, letting it travel through the air before hitting all four targets in sequence. The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course. Here, check it out:.

The clip takes place in the destroyed Hyrule Market, just before the entrance to Ganon's Castle. It's already an impressive display of precision, but what makes it even better is how unnecessary the whole thing is. Link could probably deal with those ReDeads in a much simpler way. But where's the fun in that?

It has been revealed that after its publication, the video promptly gained attention on social media, surpassing 750,000 views and 16,000 likes as we speak! Naturally, other Zelda fans were quick to praise the player's ridiculous display of skill, with one commenter calling it "one of the most impressive things I have ever seen," adding that the precision was an "absolute master class.".

Another player was equally impressed, writing, "Single-handedly the most impressive Zelda clip I ever seen." And honestly, it's hard to disagree! Pulling off a trickshot like this requires a surprising amount of patience and precision, especially when you're trying to hit multiple enemies with an arrow that wasn't even aimed directly at them.

The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course.

Recent findings suggest that what's particularly fun about this discovery is how it shows that the spirit of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom lives on even in a much more structured adventure. Ocarina of Time doesn't offer the same level of freedom when it comes to approaching combat, but that hasn't stopped players from experimenting with its mechanics and finding creative ways to play.

Sources indicate that the more recent games taught an entire generation of Zelda fans that almost every situation can become a playground if you're willing to experiment enough. Whether that's launching enemies into the air, using physics to solve problems in unexpected ways, creating weird machines, or spending far too long trying to land the perfect arrow, players have learned to make their own fun! And now, even without a single Lynel around, that same energy has found its way into Ocarina of Time. I guess some habits really do follow you from one Hyrule to another.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Organization of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge.
  • Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
  • According to recent reports, the team began planning the 3.0 enhancement two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Tech giant of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Organization of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

According to recent reports, the team began planning the 3.0 enhancement two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Tech giant of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio.".

It has been revealed that relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Company of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel says. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'.".

Sources indicate that complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added fresh units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie notes. "It was a lot.".

As the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an issue that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a upcoming Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel notes.

According to recent reports, further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the substantial 3.0 enhancement release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Organization of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 update that we had a substantial spike of customers and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well.".

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

It has been revealed that the next release for Firm of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the update, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding newly introduced units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

After that, though, I ask if Relic intends to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a new project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing.".

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

It has been revealed that on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Sources indicate that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

It has been revealed that for me, management sims always have that inevitable level of stress that just gets worse and worse as you progress. Thrifty Business, however, seems to subvert all that, as while you're tasked with managing your own thrift shop, it supposedly does so in a totally chill, totally low-pressure way.

Sources indicate that that alone is enough to pique my interest, to be honest, but couple that with its charming visuals and 90s-inspired aesthetics and I'm sold. The sim lets you unlock furniture and decor as you go along, with over 500 cosmetic items you can tinker around with - and the best part of it all is that the first 60 minutes are free for you to try!

Sources indicate that my little 12-year-old niece is, I feel, the smartest kid in the world, but even she's not capable of throwing people to the dungeons to keep her kingdom's affairs in order. In Lil' Guardsman, the eponymous Lil is tasked with exactly that, as she's left on gate guard duty by her dear ol' dad. According to recent reports, we've got another roguelike in our list this week, and I'm not complaining! Rogue Adventure is a dungeon-crawling RPG with procedurally generated elements where you combine cards and unleash epic skills onto unwitting foes to win.

Download now! PUBG Mobile Flash.

Bart Bonte is at it again with his series of colour-themed puzzlers, and this time, it's Brown that's taking the spotlight.

In a recent development, at its core, Bonte's puzzles are all about filling the entire screen with whatever colour's in the title, so for this one, you'll need to do just that across 50 levels. Some puzzles are a simple matter of putting two and two together, while others need a little bit more logic to figure out - thankfully, there's a handy hint system to help you out in case you ever get stuck!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it feels like we've already known the main GTA 6 characters for a long time now, as we've spent years seeing Jason, Lucia, and others in trailers, screenshots, and more as we gradually got more information about the game.
  • In a recent development, there have been many questions and rumors about who the GTA 6 cast members are, and players are eager to find out which actors are performing in these roles.
  • However, with the game officially launching we can finally discover who the main actors are.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it feels like we've already known the main GTA 6 characters for a long time now, as we've spent years seeing Jason, Lucia, and others in trailers, screenshots, and more as we gradually got more information about the game. Now that GTA 6 is finally here, we can actually meet them properly and discover how their roles will play out in Rockstar's epic adventure across Leonida.

In a recent development, there have been many questions and rumors about who the GTA 6 cast members are, and players are eager to find out which actors are performing in these roles. That information has previously been kept under strict NDAs, though it wasn't hard for trailer viewers to work out that Stephen Root was involved as Brian Heder, and more recently Manni L. Perez's role main role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed with a Best Performance nomination at The Game Awards.

However, with the game officially launching we can finally discover who the main actors are. There is a QR code found in the Account section of the Settings menu in-game linking to the credits on the official Rockstar website, and while that page is at the moment 404ing people were already able to obtain the details we're looking for here. With that in mind, here's what you need to know about the main GTA 6 cast and the characters they play.

Played by Dylan RourkeOne half of GTA 6's protagonist duo is Jason Duval, a troubled teen-turned-ex-soldier who "grew up around grifters and crooks." As an adult, he found himself running for drug dealers in the Florida Keys, where he soon met and started a relationship with Lucia Caminos. Their romance sounds like a tumultuous one, fueled by danger and narrow escapes as they swerve the long arm of the law at each turn. But with Jason allegedly eyeing up a more "quiet life," what does that mean for the Bonnie and Clyde of Vice City, Leonida?Dylan Rourke has appeared in reveals such as Grey's Anatomy, 9-1-1: Lone Star, Station 19, and Modern Family.

Played by Manni L. PerezScrappy and ambitious, Jason's other half Lucia Caminos is desperate to make her mother proud. Determined to live the "good life" they've yearned for since leaving Liberty City, GTA 6 sees Lucia taking a more metered approach to achieving that dream – potentially with fewer flying fists, as her official bio suggests a lifelong boxing practice that hasn't always helped keep her out of trouble. She's just come out of prison, and with Jason potentially offering an escape from a life of crime, we're left wondering how easy it would be for Lucia and Jason to leave that life in the rearview mirror.Manni L. Perez has appeared in shows such as Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, and also provided the voice for a clubber in GTA 5 and a blackjack dealer in GTA Online.

According to recent reports, played by Bobby MoynihanIt wouldn't be a GTA game without a sidekick or two, and Cal happens to be a reclusive techie to boot. Jason's buddy Cal doubles as a useful work contact, keeping an ear on restricted radio channels from the safety of his house. Described as lacking ambition "at the low tide of America," Cal would happily coast there with his mini fridge if Jason didn't have "bigger looks" for his skills. Sounds like funny business if you ask me, but maybe we'll see Jason and Lucia using Cal's comms-busting to pick up fresh missions and leads?Bobby Moynihan was a principal cast member on Saturday Night Live for almost a decade, and has appeared in NCIS: Origins, Minions & Monsters, and much more.

Recent findings suggest that played by Stephen RootA member of the old guard when it comes to drug running in the Keys, Jason's landlord Brian Heder is still a key – albeit subtle – player in the biz. He's remarked to use his boat yard for moving illegal cargo, but now on his third wife and nearing retirement age, it seems Brian has quiet criminality down to a T. He lets Jason live rent-free at one of his properties with the caveat that he roughs up the occasional heavy from time to time, but with Jason invited over for family drinks every so often, he seems more a friend than a tenant to Brian.Stephen Root is widely recognizable and has appeared in King of the Hill, Office Space, Barry, and much more.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

According to recent reports, played by Manny PerezOne of the more mysterious GTA 6 characters is Raul Bautista, a man who turns bank heists into works of art. His manipulative charm has proved invaluable over the years, with numerous high-risk bank robberies pulled off with finesse, but he's "always on the hunt for talent". With the stakes getting higher and more dangerous by the gig, though, it's hinted that Raul's "crew" might have to decide whether the payload is worth the liability – could Lucia and Jason be part of that crew?Manny Perez has appeared in Sound of Freedom, Blue Bloods, Pride and Glory, and Bella.

Played by Mike ForbsOne of the undisputed kings of Vice City's criminal underbelly, Boobie Ike is a guy with a lot of gold-encrusted fingers in a lot of pies. In GTA 6, it's clear that his myriad enterprises – a real estate business, strip club, and recording studio – are all funded by the drug trade, but he does seem to have special interest in Dre'Quan Priest, a recently-signed musician who used to perform at his strip club.Mike Forbs has appeared in Ruth & Boaz, Life is a Simulation (Patient), and Lone Star Bull.

Played by Naiqui MacabroadDre'Quan grew up as a street punk with dreams of stardom, described as "more hustler than gangster". GTA 6 sees Dre'Quan landing a partnership with rap star duo Real Dimez, and through them, a chance to be signed by Only Raw Records and quit his days moonlighting at Boobie's strip club. But what Rockstar tells us about Boobie leads us to believe he's eyeing up a cut of Dre'Quan's success, one way or another...Naiqui Macabroad has appeared in reveals such as Chicago P.D., Law & Order, and Crashing.

Played by Hood Brat (Bae-Luxe) and Krissy Celess (Roxy Rashad)Viral rap sensations Bae-Lux and Roxy Rashad are Real Dimez, a music duo looking for their next major hit to take social media by storm. Their past is hinted at being pretty shady, inspired by past altercations with drug dealers, but it's been five years since their last big number and they're looking for something even juicier to fuel their upcoming partnership with Only Raw Records. Enter: Dre'Quan, their next project. It seems both Real Dimez girls will have a lot of interplay with Boobie and Dre'Quan in GTA 6, which could speak to one of the more prominent subplots in the game.

Hood Brat and Krissy Celess are rap and hip-hop artists who collaborated on the single "F.A.B." earlier in 2026.

If you're causing chaos with this cast of characters, then here's what you need to know about GTA 6 Wanted Levels and your GTA 6 criminal profiles.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to patch the community on what to expect in 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of latest content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to patch the community on what to expect in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s newly introduced blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

Recent findings suggest that the first stage of the newly introduced roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

In a recent development, the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo concerns, and other crashes and freezing.

Industry observers note that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers problems around eating and drinking.

Sources indicate that another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more concerns join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

According to recent reports, the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next upgrade will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported challenges.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#51902. GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (822 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6.
  • This wasn't simply an overlooked feature.
  • In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6. One old activity, though, isn't making the cut. Players can no longer hire sex workers, ending a feature that's been part of the series since Grand Theft Auto 3 arrived in 2001.

This wasn't simply an overlooked feature. Rockstar deliberately left it out. Shacknews asked the GTA studio about it, and they confirmed the feature was removed. Rockstar also offered an explanation, and it comes down to the kind of story it wants to tell with Jason and Lucia.

In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run. The studio noted it had considered which familiar GTA elements would work alongside the characters and the relationship at the center of the game, rather than bringing back every previous feature by default.

In a recent development, rockstar pointed to systems such as police pursuits, radio stations, robberies, and car theft as examples of the elements it carried forward. Those all fit the criminal adventures Jason and Lucia get caught up in. Hiring sex workers, apparently, didn't fit what the team had in mind.

Sources indicate that it's an interesting explanation because Rockstar didn't claim the removal was due to a technical limitation or a ratings requirement. Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Industry observers note that anyone who's watched the GTA 6 launch trailer will have seen how much of the marketing revolves around the pair. Rockstar keeps bringing the focus back to Jason and Lucia, even when the trailers show off everything else happening in Leonida. Their story is the reason the two playable protagonists are together in the first place.

Hiring sex workers first became a recognizable open-world interaction in GTA 3, and it remained available across later mainline games, including Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5. For some players, it became one of those strange little things they expected to find when wandering around a GTA city at night.

It also brings back one of GTA 3's more infamous controversies. Players could hire a sex worker, kill her afterward, and pick up the money they'd just spent. That drew plenty of criticism at the time, and the mechanic stuck around. It was still possible in GTA 5.

I can't help connecting this to Jason Schreier's 2022 Bloomberg report, which said Rockstar was trying to avoid jokes that punch down at marginalized groups. He suggested GTA 6 might feel quite different from GTA 5, and seeing this particular feature disappear makes me think he might have been onto something. Rockstar claims it's about Jason and Lucia, of course, but I wonder if both things played a part.

It was never the reason most people played these games, of course. But GTA has always made a point of filling its streets with activities that aren't strictly necessary for completing missions. The series' reputation comes as much from those distractions as it does from car chases, shootouts, and elaborate heists.

According to recent reports, that's why removing a relatively minor interaction is still newsworthy. It has survived several generations of GTA, across different protagonists and settings. Now that Rockstar is putting two characters in a relationship at the heart of its newest game, that particular carryover has finally been dropped.

This doesn't mean GTA 6 has suddenly become a tame version of Grand Theft Auto. The game's nightlife is very much present. Our guide to GTA 6's strip clubs already covers several venues around Leonida, so the absence of one activity shouldn't be confused with the removal of adult entertainment altogether.

There's a distinction between the atmosphere of Vice City and the specific actions Rockstar lets the protagonists take. A setting can still have strip clubs and the more outrageous side of GTA without including every interaction that existed in previous games.

It has been revealed that the confirmation is also about a specific action players can take. It doesn't establish whether sex workers appear in the game as background characters, or whether the story mentions them. Rockstar answered a question about the gameplay interaction, not every possible appearance of the subject.

Some fans will probably find the change strange, particularly if they've been playing since the PS2 days. Others might not have noticed the feature was missing at all. Either way, it's one of the clearer examples of Rockstar choosing to leave an old mechanic behind instead of carrying it over simply because it's always been there.

The 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

Recent findings suggest that counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

It has been revealed that vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

It has been revealed that the suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Manufacturer’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly promptly.

According to recent reports, as it presently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

In a recent development, the concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre manufacturer who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
  • HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
  • In a recent development, the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

In a recent development, the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's upgrade.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

How To Find Dog Island In GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and it's as chaotic, grandiose, and weird as you'd expect.
  • Sources indicate that as the name suggests, it's a small island filled with lifeguard dogs that you can visit.
  • You can get to Dog Island as soon as you complete your first day as Jason, but it can also be reached on Lucia if you've progressed further into the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and it's as chaotic, grandiose, and weird as you'd expect. While there are a comical number of secrets and hidden interactions you can discover, one of the oddest is Dog Island.

Sources indicate that as the name suggests, it's a small island filled with lifeguard dogs that you can visit. However, finding it will require getting lost, but it's worth the effort if you're just starting. Here is everything you need to know about reaching Dog Island and what you'll get for your troubles.

You can get to Dog Island as soon as you complete your first day as Jason, but it can also be reached on Lucia if you've progressed further into the campaign. Once you wake up at his house and finish getting ready, go out to the nearby dock and get into his boat. Now we need to head out to open water, so go west from Key Lento into Leonide Bay.

When you arrive, look for any open spot of water, kill your boat's engines, and jump in the water. Start swimming away from your boat. After around 20–30 seconds of swimming, you will hear barking. Activate your Focus Mode to locate the source of the noise, which is a dog in a life vest driving a jet ski.

This is Cool Dog, and he functions as a way to get back to shore if you're stranded or your boat is destroyed. Approach Cool Dog, hold down L2 to focus on him, and then select the Praise option when you meet him. This will allow Jason to climb onto Cool Dog's jet ski.

Once you do, sit back and relax as Cool Dog brings you to shore. However, if you stick with Cool Dog he will eventually bring you to Dog Island, which is located in the southern portion of the Grassrivers region. How long this takes depends entirely on where Cool Dog picks you up, which is why I suggest doing it early, since Jason's first home is right by the Grassrivers.

You'll know you've reached Dog Island, as Cool Dog will get off the jet ski and join a few other dogs under an overturned boat. When you arrive, there are a couple of things you can find. The first is a wallet that Cool Dog will dig up for you, which contains 1,200 dollars. Cool Dog will carry it around in his mouth, so approach him to get this newly introduced furry friend to drop the wallet for you!

Industry observers note that this is a nice amount of cash to start you off if you visit Dog Island early. Additionally, there will be the Sports Wrap Shade sunglasses you can snag in the small hole to the left of the boat near the toys. Picking them up will automatically equip the glasses for Jason and will permanently add them to his wardrobe.

Recent findings suggest that you should make sure to throw either the Frisbee or mini-football for the dogs on the island, as this will make progress towards increasing your Focus meter. It won't be a lot, but every little bit counts, and who doesn't want to play with all the cute dogs running around anyway?

It has been revealed that when you're ready to leave, you can actually just take Cool Dog's jet ski. It's quite fast, and he doesn't seem to mind you borrowing it! Don't worry about your boat either, as it will respawn back at your house free of charge. While that's all you can do on Dog Island, Cool Dog will still be around to rescue you if you're ever stranded at sea, so just make sure to listen for the barking!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christopher Nolan usually waits a few years before releasing another project, but just a few months after The Odyssey hit screens this summer and became the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever, he's already thinking about this next movie.

"He’s mulling some stuff," remarked Nolan's longtime collaborator and life partner Emma Thomas to The Playlist. "He’s thinking. He’s not very good at doing nothing, so he’s thinking about it. But no, we don’t know what it is going to be exactly yet.".

When asked if there is going to be the same three-year gap between The Odyssey and Nolan's next project, as there was between the 2026 movie and 2023's Oppenheimer, Thomas noted, "I don’t know. Now I feel like it might be longer, but then again, as I said, he’s not very good at twiddling his thumb[s].".

Industry observers note that if Nolan does indeed need a break, that is very understandable, as The Odyssey is no doubt one of his biggest projects to date. The movie was shot in various countries and remote places, from remote caves in Greece to the open sea, where Nolan got through 400 miles of film. Thomas worked as a producer on The Odyssey, but took a very hands-on approach, being on set in the thick of it in even the harshest conditions. "This was definitely the most complicated [project I have worked on]," added Thomas.

The Oscar-winning producer has worked on many of her husband's projects from Memento to The Dark Knight trilogy. Though she admits she does "get excited when I hear about other people’s challenges," she thinks she will stick to working with Nolan. "I have such a great thing going with Chris. I’m honestly so lucky working with him. He’s spoiled me completely because he’s as demanding as he is of everybody around him and of himself; he’s also incredibly pragmatic. And inventive.".

Though Thomas says Nolan is pragmatic and less likely to work on many projects at once, she clarifies, "It’s not like he’s saying to me, 'I think I’m just going to put my feet up and take a break.' That’s not happening anytime soon. So I feel like there’s a lot to do, and I’m very lucky to have that partnership. And there’s not really room for anything else within that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Recent findings suggest that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

The club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

Industry observers note that his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

It has been revealed that that deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

According to recent reports, A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

5 years of memories. it was an honour to see you grow into the person and player you are 🧡 https://t.co/F3TWY9WZqq pic.twitter.com/K3K3EQICZ1.

According to recent reports, for the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert states Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The fresh hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

Losing progress in a game is never fun, but imagine spending 11 hours exploring Grand Theft Auto 6 only to discover that none of it was saved. That's exactly what happened to content creator JasonTheWeen, who had a particularly rough launch day after making one unfortunate mistake with his PlayStation 5.

In a recent development, with around 1.3 million followers on YouTube, the content creator had been streaming an extended session of Rockstar's latest adventure. However, after accidentally turning off his console, he returned to the game only to find that his entire 11-hour save was missing!

It has been revealed that according to The Economic Times, he later explained that his foot had accidentally hit the switch on an extension cord, cutting power to his PS5. The moment he realized what had happened was captured live, and his reaction was understandably heartbreaking. Here, take a look:.

Industry observers note that visibly devastated, the streamer struggled to hold back tears and repeatedly shouted about the 11 hours he had just lost. He then contacted someone from his team to ask whether there was any way to recover his progress, even if that meant getting back to the beginning of the second chapter rather than having to start the entire adventure again.

Unfortunately, it seems that it wasn’t possible, and he eventually brought a friend to help him rush through the sections he had already completed, hoping to get his marathon back on track.

The exact reason behind the incident remains unclear, but there's a possible explanation involving the game's save system. GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain key events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

One possibility is that JasonTheWeen accidentally turned off his PS5 while the game was writing save data. If that happened, interrupting the process could have corrupted the save file, potentially explaining why so much progress disappeared when he released the game again.

GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain important events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

According to recent reports, it's important to stress that this is only a theory, and neither Rockstar nor the streamer has confirmed what actually caused the loss. We also don't know whether the save can be recovered, so it would be unfair to draw conclusions about the game's autosave system based on this single incident.

Still, the situation is a good reminder that manually saving your progress is worth the extra few seconds. GTA 6 offers multiple manual save slots, allowing players to keep separate backups instead of relying exclusively on autosaving. This can be particularly useful after completing a long mission or spending hours exploring Leonida.

For anyone planning to sink an entire afternoon into the game, taking a moment to create a manual save might save you from a very unpleasant surprise later!

Industry observers note that unfortunately, losing his progress wasn't the only upsetting moment JasonTheWeen experienced during the stream. Shortly afterward, he heard shouting outside his home and informed viewers that police officers had arrived at his property.

Sources indicate that the incident appears to have been a case of swatting, a dangerous prank involving false emergency reports intended to send police officers to someone's home. It's an especially unpleasant situation for any streamer, and it made an already frustrating day considerably worse.

Industry observers note that following the incident, JasonTheWeen also reached out to Rockstar and Sony on social media, asking whether his lost progress could be recovered. For now, there's no confirmed response from either manufacturer about his request or why all the progress was lost.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another upcoming entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet latest characters.

Sources indicate that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

According to recent reports, the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

Sources indicate that you can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game rolls out. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their aims for the shooter making some major promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

It has been revealed that the previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few upcoming weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, major ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is at the moment slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).
