💡 Key Takeaways
  • The question comes up plenty as online games proliferate and once-great studios are devastated by layoffs in a frequently changing, shifting industry.
  • After all, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives after a 13-year wait… but where is GTA 6 Online?
  • The state of single-player gaming can wax and wane, and it's been a hot topic of conversation ever since EA themselves declared them "finished" back in 2010, back when live service was beginning to dominate and almost every single-player game had a multiplayer component of some sort.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Are single-player games dead? The question comes up plenty as online games proliferate and once-great studios are devastated by layoffs in a frequently changing, shifting industry. But, as many games dodge roll out of the gaming crater that is November thanks to GTA 6's launch – there's also never been a better time to celebrate the single-player game, and what a massive success they can still be.

After all, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives after a 13-year wait… but where is GTA 6 Online? Not here, that's what, and that hasn't stopped Rockstar Games' latest from already raking in an estimated $1.45 billion even in its all-digital form. It's not the only one this month, as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake became the best-selling physical game of 2026 in the US after just one week on shelves – another single-player adventure.

The state of single-player gaming can wax and wane, and it's been a hot topic of conversation ever since EA themselves declared them "finished" back in 2010, back when live service was beginning to dominate and almost every single-player game had a multiplayer component of some sort.

In our GTA 6 review, we call it " the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation" with a great single-player story to follow.

Sources indicate that it's a sentiment that's been hit back on over the years with plenty of massive single-player success. Larian Studios' head Swen Vinke has even explicitly called out the line of thinking, saying the style of game isn't dead, and that "they just have to be good." Likewise, plenty of solo-focused indie games are successful, and left out of an often AAA-dominated conversation.

Even so, the idea that 'single-player games are dying' has been hard to escape within an industry plagued by layoffs recently. Especially with the sad closure of EA-owned RPG giant BioWare last month, the developer of legendary offline adventures who ended up in the live service mines with Anthem and early versions of Dragon Age: The Veilguard. There's a sense that EA might be part of a self-fulfilling prophecy with their original observation.

But, Vinke is correct – games being good certainly help, and few are better than GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time remake. GTA 6 even shares a Metacritic ranking with the original Ocarina of Time, sitting at 99 to be the joint highest rated games ever. It doesn't get much better than that.

It's heartening to see big investments like GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time remake pay off.

It's heartening to see big investments like GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time remake pay off. Even if they're such gigantic cultural icons that it feels obvious that players would show up, it's still not something I take completely for granted. I hope that those logging back in for single-player adventures like these two will stick around and remember the joys of solo play for other, less obvious games once they're looking for more. And, even though they're both games in well-known series, I'm also pleased at just how different GTA 6 and Ocarina are while still both finding recent success – a mature crime caper sandbox and a fairy tale adventure for kids (and big kids like me).

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It has been revealed that it all comes after a series of reflective moments about the sustainability of huge online gaming. PlayStation's huge push to spin up multiple live service online games continues to flounder as Fairgames joins its online gaming graveyard.

Sure, I've had plenty of great gaming moments playing with friends deep into the night. But, equally precious to me are the times I've been lost in digital worlds on my own, the flickering of a TV pulling me into deep immersion with characters, worlds, and stories that have left a mark on my own soul, that I reflect on day-to-day. The joy of gaming as a medium is the breadth of experiences they can offer, resonating with me just like a good movie or book could while also providing spaces to chill out with pals.

Industry observers note that so, is single-player gaming dead? Not even close. This November, it's more alive than ever.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next major game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

Recent findings suggest that the Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Sources indicate that immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game swiftly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

In a recent development, these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Industry observers note that like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a significant launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

Where To Easily Find Planes And Helicopters In GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's open world of Leonida is easily one of the biggest and most detailed maps in all of gaming history, and it can be pretty tough to get around and see it all.
  • It has been revealed that like previous games in the series, one of the best ways to travel is through the air via airplanes and helicopters.
  • Recent findings suggest that let's start off with the slightly more challenging planes, which are scattered around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's open world of Leonida is easily one of the biggest and most detailed maps in all of gaming history, and it can be pretty tough to get around and see it all.

It has been revealed that like previous games in the series, one of the best ways to travel is through the air via airplanes and helicopters. While there are some dangerous routes, you're best off finding some reliable locations.

Recent findings suggest that let's start off with the slightly more challenging planes, which are scattered around Leonida. Unlike previous GTA games, you can travel anywhere on the map without difficulty from the start of GTA 6, so we're not stuck in the Keys looking for a rogue airport. A great starting location is the area shown on the map above near Port Gellhorn, which has a small runway that you can easily get a plane from. You can also easily get a plane from the entrance to Southwind, near the starting Keys area.

Sources indicate that for a more surprising choice, head over to the housing area just above Bellville. This might seem like a weird place to find some planes, but many of the wealthy owners have easily stealable planes waiting in their driveway. Coming here at night is a reliable way of getting a plane without going through too much trouble.

If you're feeling brave, Vice City International Airport is a good choice for getting both massive and small planes, although you'll need to be very sneaky to avoid all of the police presence and security. It's not an instant five stars anymore, though, so it's less of a gamble than it used to be if you're playing smartly.

Industry observers note that on that note, avoid Mile Zero Air Station to the West of the Keys, as it's a military base with some really powerful enemies. Even in the endgame, this is a massive risk that's not really worth it.

It has been revealed that while planes are a little easier to take on long-haul flights around Leonida, they can also be a pain to get in the air. That's not the case for helicopters, and they're arguably a lot easier to find once you know what to look for. A great starting location is Southwind in the Southwest part of the map, close to the Keys where you start the game.

It has been revealed that right on the docks of Southwind is a helicopter pad that can have a wirlybird spawned for you. Considering how close it is to where Jason starts the game, it's a great choice with low risk, despite it being right next to the Mile Zero Air Station. It's not a guarantee of a helicopter, but it's a good bet.

Industry observers note that another great location is the Southside medical centre, as shown on the map above. This hospital has a helipad on its roof, and it can easily be reached by going to the left of the building and taking the stairs up. The helicopter that spawns here is usually unlocked and has no tracker, so it's a very safe bet for getting up in the skies early on in your playthrough.

Recent findings suggest that there are also helipads on many of Vice City's tallest buildings, but getting up there in the first place might require an aircraft. These also tend to come with advanced trackers, so it's a bit more of a risk.

Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” notes game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

According to recent reports, in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override releases in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

Industry observers note that the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, bringing with it an avalanche of rave reviews and jokes about creative excuses to miss work. Unfortunately, for many Ubisoft workers, the drive home today will also be their last one.

Recent findings suggest that according to Jon Hicks of GamesIndustry.biz, French gaming giant Ubisoft has dropped the guillotine on 166 roles in Canada, concentrated in the company’s Québec and Montreal studios. Ubisoft attributes the move to matching its resources with “current production priorities and business needs.”.

Ubisoft notes workers affected “are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources” to help smooth out the ride.

Since the announcing of a joint venture between Ubisoft and Tencent, and a major restructuring proposal that comes with it, the company has gone through a turbulent period to try and align its workforce with the newly-set goals. As has become the norm, this has come at the expense of workers.

Industry observers note that the terminated roles appear to represent approximately 4% of the affected studios’ workforce, primarily in support and production positions, a testament to just how massive Ubisoft’s Canadian operation has gotten over the years. Earlier this year, Ubisoft closed down its Halifax studio in Nova Scotia.

Industry observers note that ubisoft has not commented on specific projects affected, but Jon Hicks claims some of the workers laid off were part of Vantage Studios. Previously known as Creative House 1, Vantage Studios focuses on the company’s significant money titles, namely the Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six, and Far Cry franchises.

Layoffs have left a dark stain in the gaming industry for a while now, especially as companies have begun overcorrecting for the post-lockdown hiring spree.

Industry observers note that according to Ubisoft, the company is finally seeing the light as it closes in on the targeted €200 million in savings (approximately $220 million as of today). Unfortunately, just as the French company is about to leave the meat grinder, its Microsoft peers across the Atlantic are just getting started.

The company has gone through a turbulent period to try and align its workforce with the newly-set goals. As has become the norm, this has come at the expense of workers.

XBOX CEO Asha Sharma has been on a mission to try and save the manufacturer after years of falling behind against its Sony competitors. However, the road to a long-term vision for a sustainable, successful XBOX brand also seems to go through the rough parts of town, namely divestments and layoffs that have so far cost us iconic studios like Hellblade’s Ninja Theory.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, California-based Electronic Arts brought the hammer down on BioWare last month, in a move that was equal parts shocking and predictable. The studio was known to be struggling even before its parent tech giant’s acquisition by a Saudi public investment fund became official earlier this year, and it appears EA felt we don’t need a upcoming Mass Effect when there’s Star Wars in the making.

Recent findings suggest that the next release from Ubisoft’s Vantage Studios is set to be a newly introduced spin on Rainbow Six, called Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Tactics. The game will be a single-player tactics game that brings the franchise back to its more grounded roots as a counter-terrorism simulator, with the 2027 release window set to ride the wave of Star Wars: Zero Manufacturer.

Rainbow Six Tactics looks to tick all the boxes of what franchise oldheads have been waiting for, but according to an insider, there is an even bigger nostalgia bomb in the works. As reported by Insider Gaming, Ubisoft is quietly working on a sequel to Rainbow Six: Vegas under the codename Spades.

Industry observers note that my first brush with Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six was with Lockdown back in the glory days of the PlayStation 2, a game developed by the now-defunct Red Storm Entertainment and Ubisoft Montreal. Indie spiritual successors like Ready or Not have scratched that itch to some extent, but I know I'm not alone in yearning for that with AAA polish again.

For now, we can only hope both the Tactics and Vegas 3 teams will survive the final round of cuts as Ubisoft finds its footing again.

"If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two newly introduced destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two latest features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Industry observers note that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature releases, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a newly introduced virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

According to recent reports, it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

According to recent reports, in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

It has been revealed that in the blog post announcing the upcoming features, Maxis remarked that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Knowing whether you can pet animals in GTA 6 should be one of the first questions you ask yourself, as it should in any game with animals in, to be honest. And, as ever, there's loads of wildlife in GTA 6 - though despite how it might sound above, I don't suggest you try and pet the alligators.Dogs and cats, though, can absolutely be played with and, provided you're making an effort to win Lucia back, you may come across one of the cutest cats we've ever seen pretty early on in Chapter 1, though it's not obvious how to interact with them. So, don't get too distracted, but here's how to pet animals in GTA 6.

To pet animals in GTA 6, you need to approach them and press L2 or LT, which gives you the option to praise them. Praise them a few times and you'll finally see the option to pet them, though this doesn't always work.

This is effectively the same as interacting with NPCs, but the option doesn't appear in the bottom of the screen for animals, meaning it's not so clear how to do so. By pressing L2 or LT on an unidentified animal also gives you the option to 'Study' them, which is the only way to add them to your collection of all the GTA 6 animals. You might also see the option to 'Scold' them, but we don't do that. Ever.

Of course you won't be able to pet all animals, just the domesticated ones, but there are different breeds to find, so do make sure you interact with, study, and of course pet every dog and cat you see. The one seen in the images above are of the adorable grocery store employee that you'll find in Key Lento Mini Mart, so go stock up on supplies and meet them while you're at it. In fact, if you're working on improving your GTA 6 relationship status with Lucia, you should pick up some groceries before picking her up from jail. If you've already missed this, good luck making it up to her.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

It has been revealed that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony mentioned that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring upcoming creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

In a recent development, sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

According to recent reports, for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that A newly-discovered document from the Australian Classification Board has leaked the existence of a fresh Fallout spin-off game titled A Wasteland Full of Cats.
  • Is it the Fallout game we’ve all been waiting for in the near-decade since the launch of Fallout 76?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, here’s a fun fact: in the lore of the Fallout series, dogs weren’t allowed into the Vault-Tec Vaults, with all the dogs we see throughout the games being those that survived and evolved into wolf-like forms after the Great War. Cats, on the other hand, were permitted into the Vaults within reason thanks to their applications as therapy pets and efficacy as pest-hunters. In spite of that, cats didn’t start appearing in the Fallout games until Fallout 4 and Fallout 76. Apparently, the reason for that is that they all just sorta got lost somewhere.

Sources indicate that A newly-discovered document from the Australian Classification Board has leaked the existence of a fresh Fallout spin-off game titled A Wasteland Full of Cats. This game is apparently being created in cooperation between Bethesda and Devcats, an indie developer specializing in hidden object games about cats like A Park Full of Cats, A Building Full of Cats, and An Arcade Full of Cats.

Is it the Fallout game we’ve all been waiting for in the near-decade since the launch of Fallout 76? No, definitely not, but, well, it’s something, I suppose. Every bit of Fallout-adjacent content we get can continue to tide us over until Fallout 5, whenever that ends up being, or at least the next season of the Fallout television series.

It has been revealed that according to the description of the game on the Australian Classification Board website, A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults that dot the Wasteland. Following some manner of accident, all of the other cats living in the Vault alongside you are let loose out into the Wasteland, and you’ll need to go out there to round them all up.

In the same vein as Devcats’s other games, this will be a jaunt through 14 locations and 33 rooms where you’ll need to point out the errant cats hidden within the scenery, Where’s Waldo-style.

A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults.

You’ll be helped along the way by various NPC characters, hopefully including some familiar faces, with many of the locations you visit apparently being classic spots from across the Fallout franchise. Some of these locations will have mild puzzle elements, allowing you to uncover non-critical secret levels. According to the description, the game will culminate in a final battle against a horde of Radroaches, though I’m admittedly not quite sure how finding cats translates into battling giant mutant roaches, but I guess we’ll find out.

It has been an exceptionally hot minute since the last mainline Fallout game, specifically the release of Fallout 4 in 2015. Since then, it’s been pretty much exclusively spin-offs, such as the mobile title Fallout Shelter, its gacha-added version, Fallout Shelter Online, the MMO stylings of Fallout 76, and I guess Zen Pinball’s Fallout table for the Pinball FX games, if you want to count that.

Back in 2022, Todd Howard noted in an interview with IGN that development on Fallout 5 would begin in earnest once The Elder Scrolls VI was done and dusted. Of course, considering we only just learned that game’s full title recently, I have a sinking feeling the timeline has shifted on that a bit. For what it’s worth, Bethesda did say in an X, formerly Twitter post this past July that Fallout 5 has officially begun pre-production, but again, that doesn’t give us much to go on.

Sources indicate that as of now, we don’t have any particular release dates or even release windows for upcoming Fallout projects, whether it’s mainline games, the TV show, or even this new cat thing. Just gotta keep wading through the Wasteland patiently, I guess….

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, RayNeo.

Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4 has a themed pair of AR glasses with industry-leading specs, and they go on sale November 19.

According to recent reports, the number that matters is 307. That is how many inches across the virtual screen runs, roughly the size of a cinema wall, hanging a few metres in front of you, in a room that doesn't contain a television.

The big screen is just the start. These glasses have spatial tracking built into the hardware rather than borrowed from your console, dedicated Zone 360 silicon running native 3DoF, so the picture stays pinned where you put it, and holding it there costs you nothing out of your 120Hz frame budget. The 59° field of view is category-leading, and it is the reason a screen this size doesn't collapse into a squint at the corners.

Here is the part that tends to get missed. All three of these features belong to the standard RayNeo GT Max as well - and that model is $335 this Black Friday, down from $429.

Sources indicate that which brings us back to the pair with Call of Duty on them. The RayNeo GT Max Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4 Limited Edition takes every one of those specs and wraps them in a collector's treatment: sandblasted digital camo and an in-lens interface built for this edition and no other. It is $449, and it lands the same day.

So there are two of them. The first question for either is what you need to own to use one, and the answer is less than you would think.

There is a stubborn assumption that AR glasses are a PC accessory. It is wrong, and the Switch 2 is the proof.

Let's start with the easy case anyway. If you play on a PC or a handheld, all you need is a USB-C cable carrying DisplayPort video out. That covers most phones, laptops, and handhelds built in the past five years, so long as the USB-C port carries video. Run it from the device to the glasses, and the big screen is there in under a minute. The GT Max handles most major handhelds, the AYN Thor, Steam Deck, ROG Ally, and Legion Go among them.

Industry observers note that consoles take one more piece, and that is the whole difference. PS5 and Xbox Series owners need the RayNeo HDMI 2.0 Adapter, presently $50 rather than its usual $64. Switch 2 owners need the RayNeo JoyDock, which the console sits in and charges from while you play, down to $69 from $89 this Black Friday.

In a recent development, if you are buying the glasses and the dock together anyway, the GT Max and JoyDock bundle is $410 instead of $518 - $108 off, and the best route from a Switch 2 to a 307-inch screen. Every GT series purchase also comes with a Lens Shade at no charge.

So the hardware is not the obstacle, but is a screen that big actually good to play on?

According to recent reports, size is the easy part. Plenty of wearable displays will throw an enormous image at you and leave you squinting at the corners of it.

What stops that here is width. The GT Max runs a category-leading 59° field of view out of RayNeo's Peacock Optical Engine 3.0 Max, and that peripheral room is what turns 307 inches from a party trick into something you can play on. The edges of the minimap stay where your eyes can find them. You can change the size of the screen too, if 307 inches is too immersive for you.

It has been revealed that the rest of the panel keeps pace. These are 120Hz tournament-grade micro-OLEDs at 1,200 nits perceived brightness, 38 PPD, 98% DCI-P3 coverage, with TÜV Rheinland triple eye-comfort certification for sessions that run long. Spatial tracking is hardware-native 3DoF on dedicated Zone 360 silicon, so pinning the screen in place costs the console or PC nothing in frames. Audio is a quad-speaker array co-tuned by Bang & Olufsen on a racetrack architecture, equalised for the positional cues that decide tight matches.

Sources indicate that what all of that adds up to is less like strapping a screen to your face and more like bringing your controller to the movie theatre. The picture sits a few metres out rather than against your eyes, and in Pinned Mode it stays exactly where you put it — turn your head and the room moves while the screen holds still.

Which leaves only the decision of which pair to buy.

The standard RayNeo GT Max is $335 for Black Friday, down from $429. That is the lowest these gaming glasses have gone, and it holds through November 30. On December 1, it returns to $429. Early access has been running on RayNeo.com since November 10.

According to recent reports, the Limited Edition arrives the same day, on RayNeo.com and Amazon US, at $449 - and it concedes nothing to the standard model on paper. Same category-leading 59° field of view, same 120Hz micro-OLED panels, same hardware-native 3DoF, same Bang & Olufsen tuning. This is the flagship in a different finish, not a licensed reskin of something lesser.

What it adds is a sandblasted digital camo shell, reinforced braided video cabling, and a co-branded microfiber cloth, designed as a set rather than applied as a decal. The part that earns the name is the user interface. The standard GT Max menu is replaced by a black-and-gold on-screen display built for this edition and no other: brightness, 3D display, dynamic quality, colour enhancement and Scene Mode all sit in the lens, and you move between Standard, Movie, Eye Care and Read profiles mid-match without leaving the game or reaching for a phone. A tactical HUD readout holds display status in your peripheral vision throughout. Licensed editions usually stop at the paint. This one went into the software.

Sources indicate that the two are on different clocks, and that is the thing to weigh. The $449 is the Limited Edition's launch price rather than a Black Friday discount, so it will not drop during the sale and it will not rise on December 1 — what bounds it is the run itself, which is finite by design. The standard GT Max is the opposite: made to order, but $335 only until November 30.

Neither is a gamble on an unknown. RayNeo shipped more AR glasses than anyone in the world over the first half of 2026 — 24.8% of the global market per IDC, 23.9% per Counterpoint Research. The standard GT Max will still be there on December 1, at $429. The Limited Edition may not be there at all.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the significant Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

According to recent reports, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

In a recent development, starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

According to recent reports, if you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a fresh event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

It has been revealed that elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a fresh activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

Sources indicate that the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

In a recent development, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

It has been revealed that the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a newly introduced item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the fresh season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

Recent findings suggest that the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

In a recent development, the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Rings of Power season 3 has been building up to Sauron's forging of the One Ring for a while now, and it's finally due to debut in episode 7.
  • According to recent reports, at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+, JD Payne, who created the show with Patrick McKay, contextualizes Sauron's mission to craft the One Ring.
  • Payne goes on to explain that Galadriel plays a part in this for Sauron too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Rings of Power season 3 has been building up to Sauron's forging of the One Ring for a while now, and it's finally due to debut in episode 7. However, one of the showrunners has confirmed that it's not just a tactical move for the Dark Lord, but a personal one too.

According to recent reports, at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+, JD Payne, who created the show with Patrick McKay, contextualizes Sauron's mission to craft the One Ring. "We flash forward five years from the end of season two, and he's already taken over lots of Middle-earth," he explains. "His armies have conquered many things, but he can't conquer the two Elven realms because of the three Elven rings that are protecting them. And so, forging the One Ring is going to be the key towards him finally getting what he wants, and really this season is about exploring what that means for him.".

Payne goes on to explain that Galadriel plays a part in this for Sauron too. "We always knew he wanted to conquer and be able to rule the three Elven rings, the seven Dwarven rings, the nine rings for Men. But this season, you have to understand a little bit more about what that means from a character point of view.".

"That conquering the Elven rings isn't just about an abstract political goal, but there's a personal part of it as well," he adds. "As Celebrimbor taunts him early on and says that without the One Ring, he'll never be capable of mastering her, speaking of Galadriel, and that's a relationship we spent two years really building up.".

Recent findings suggest that the moment Payne is referencing comes in season 3's opening episode, 'Marnûkh'. After another failed attempt at forging the ring, Celebrimbor visits Sauron in a vision. "You took part in the forging of the Seven, and of the Nine, but the Three you had no hand in," he says. "Without knowing their secrets you will never create a ring capable of mastering them, of mastering her. How does that feel, knowing that the conquests that you so desire will forever elude your grasp?".

According to recent reports, it certainly seems that everything really boils down to Galadriel for Sauron, which is something that Charlie Vickers teased to GamesRadar+ ahead of season 3. He told us Sauron is "frustrated" because Galadriel remains "beyond his reach".

For more on the upcoming One Ring sequence, take a look at our exclusive deep dive into the "most complex" thing the show has ever done.

Sources indicate that the Rings of Power season 3 has two episodes remaining. Make sure you don't miss anything with our The Rings of Power season 3 release schedule and check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review for why you should be watching.

Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. Recent findings suggest that there are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
  • Recent findings suggest that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Recent findings suggest that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

Sources indicate that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

According to recent reports, the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside latest Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the major day.

Sources indicate that it's all or nothing in Outfit7's latest update for Talking Tom Gold Run, where the concept of "high risk, high return" has never been truer! In particular, a upcoming Extraction Mode within the endless runner tasks you with running faster and faster for better and better rewards - the catch is that when you crash and burn, so does your hard-earned haul.

According to recent reports, the limited-time event not only challenges your quick reflexes but also your prudence - do you go for the bigger pay-off or leave while you can with what you already have? Industry observers note that the thing is, if you choose to keep going, the faster the run gets, making obstacles trickier to dodge. Industry observers note that there's a handy Save Me option you can opt for when you fail, giving you a chance to revive and continue your run. It's a true test of tapping talent, so it's only fitting you get four upcoming outfits to go along with it!

Tang Suit Ginger, Mooncake Ginger, Moonlight Angela and Hanfu Angela join in to spice up the theming, so if you'd like to look the part while dashing through the latest mode, now's your chance.

Latest Update: 10 Details That Show GTA 6 Deserves Game of the Year

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.
  • In a recent development, the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee.
  • This has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.

In a recent development, the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee. In fact, it was nominated for more than just Game of the Year.

This has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees. Let’s break down why this long-awaited title deserves Game of the Year.

Rockstar is known for adding some great music to games. GTA 5 has a pretty great soundtrack, with it featuring numerous artists. Because of that, it was no surprise that Rockstar started announcing various artists for GTA 6.

Sources indicate that the radio is stacked with some amazing musicians who took the time to write fresh songs specifically for the game. With so much talent, it is difficult not to get lost in the beat, so long as you are someone who enjoys each artist’s music.

In the end, users recognize that this talent isn’t just for show, and the music in GTA 6 fits the vibe of the crime-forward series, making it feel more alive.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. Ever since Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, people have been asking for the next game in the series. Well, over the course of those 13 years, Rockstar has been working hard.

The team has been busting their butts to develop GTA 6 and make it as massive as possible. They have talked about how they created new systems, enhanced older ones, and added a ton of detail into their newest game.

With this much effort put in, there is no denying that the team deserves some recognition, and just being nominated reveals that people care.

Recent findings suggest that for a long time, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the record for being the highest rated game of all time with a 99 on MetaCritic. Now that reviews for GTA 6 are out, it shares the same score as Ocarina of Time.

With that being noted, there were 22 professional reviews for Ocarina of Time, and over 150 for GTA 6, so GTA 6 has a more accurate representation from multiple parties, putting it above Ocarina of Time.

That isn’t a fluke. You can look at a few review scores, see a 10/10 and write it off, but when there are over 100 different people giving it the same score or something similar, that isn’t a coincidence.

Industry observers note that there are many people, who, when they purchase a game, are in it for the visual aspect. There is nothing wrong with this, and with the advancement of graphics engines, it has become commonplace for games to try and look lifelike.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has some of the best visuals of any game that has been released this year, and even in the last decade. The developers at Rockstar spend a lot of time trying to make every shot look as cinematic as possible.

The result of this, is one of the most beautiful games to come out in a very long time, and it will hold up for many years to come. The only slight downside is the 30fps, but that is a small price to pay for this level of beauty.

Rockstar has spent ages working on GTA 6, and a major part of that work has gone into making the world feel more alive rather than a sandbox that you can run and gun in like it was in GTA 5. Previous titles didn’t respect you being a character in the world, but rather let you do whatever you wanted.

NPCs have received a major overhaul in GTA 6, reacting more to you being in the world, and turning the game into a major life sim where people will get angry with you if you pull a gun, run away in fear, and much more.

In addition to this, there are tons of activities to take part in, so much so that you can ignore the main quest for ages and still have plenty to do. You definitely won’t get bored with this game.

Instead of focusing on fleshing out three individual characters, this time around Rockstar decided to focus on creating a couple. Their names are Jason and Lucia, and their story is powerful, and they are far more fleshed out than characters in the previous game.

According to recent reports, jason and Lucia are madly in love, and they will do anything to stand by one another. The Bonnie and Clyde dynamic fits the location of Vice City very well, and it is a story that many didn’t think would work at first.

This type of emphasis on building a relationship is something that we haven’t seen in a while, and Rockstar made it work very well, meaning it is a game that will be remembered for a long time.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar is known for making some incredible characters, and GTA 6 is no exception to this. From the beginning to the end, there are numerous characters that you meet that have a lasting effect on the story and some that are only there for a moment but leave an impression.

According to recent reports, think about your time with GTA 5 and how it was fun interacting with the game’s characters. They made you laugh, and they certainly are remembered.

Recent findings suggest that well, GTA 6 has that and then some, with a cast of side characters that each have a standout personality that will make you remember them for some time to come. It shows that the devs knew what they were doing when creating the world of Leonida.

Recent findings suggest that if there is something that the Rockstar devs understand it is comedy. There was so much of it baked into GTA 5 that it was difficult to avoid. Now that same energy has been carried over to GTA 6 and it is fantastic.

If you are a fan of satire then be prepared to see it everywhere in GTA 6 because nearly everything is a satirical take on a company, person, or event.

Sources indicate that rockstar devs are masters of comedic timing and satire, and GTA 6 proves it. It is a game that will have you chuckling at the references and laughing at the absurdity. It hits the funny bone and there is no denying that that plays a major role in why it is so good.

Something that I like in games is when you can edit your character in some way. I like to make my own character or dress up existing characters in fun outfits, and GTA 6 has that and then some.

Industry observers note that similar to previous games in the series, there are numerous outfits that you can purchase for your characters, which is a dream for those who like to customize their look. On top of that, you can edit your cars, and you can also edit your appearance through working out.

Recent findings suggest that that’s right. The game is detailed enough that Lucia and Jason will gain weight, their hair will grow long, and more. You can spend time truly focusing on your character’s appearance, and that is something I want out of my game of the year.

In a recent development, let’s be honest, there are many games that are released that are buggy messes. For instance, massive games like Crimson Desert and Assassin’s Creed Shadows had some massive glitches that hurt the games when they were first released.

Industry observers note that it took some rather large patches to fix them, and even then there were still problems. GTA 6 is one of the few games that have been released that has little to no issues with it, and in 2026, that is a massive feat, especially for a game with the the scope of GTA 6.

The lack of issues with the game at launch with how massive it is makes it a much more enticing pick for Game of the Year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida isn't just the biggest map that Rockstar Games has ever made, as it's also full to the brim with unique and detailed locations for the player to stumble upon.

Recent findings suggest that one of the memorable optional locations in Vice City is one that fans have been talking about ever since it was originally spotted - the Vice City Oceanarium. Here's where you can find it.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6's take on one of Florida's many aquariums (most likely Orlando's SeaWorld, let's be real) can be found on Barentine Drive, to the East of the Catalan Key. You'll know you're in the right place when you see signage for the aquarium, as well as its signature domelike structures that can be easily spotted throughout Vice City and by looking at the map.

It has been revealed that as you would hope, the Oceanarium is home to some unique aquatic life, including flamingos, manatees, and an orca. Those last two are noteworthy, as my many hours in Leonida suggest that they can actually only be found in the Oceanarium, making it an essential visit if you're trying to scan every animal.

Sources indicate that if you visit at night, you can even get into the tank and swim around with the Oceanarium's inhabitants. I never tried it during the day, but I can't imagine it goes down well with the staff.

Beyond being one of the most impressively detailed locations in Grand Theft Auto 6, the Oceanarium actually has a point to it, as visiting the entrance at night reveals a whole sidequest centred around protestors. As far as I can tell, there's nothing that points you to the Oceanarium and its side quest, making it one of the game's more easily missable missions.

Spider-Man Brand Latest Day director Destin Daniel Cretton had "one meeting" with Marvel about Spider-Man: Homecoming but it "didn't go anywhere.".

“Yeah, I had one meeting on Spider-Man: Homecoming. They were meeting a bunch of directors at that time I went in and met with producer Jeremy Latcham," Cretton revealed to Empire. "And it was a conversation that didn't go anywhere because I didn't really have a pitch. But that was my only interaction until I went in to seriously pitch for Shang-Chi.”.

Not only is that a fascinating insight into a sliding doors moment that eventually saw Cretton helm the most successful Spider-Man movie of all time (with over $2.5 billion at the box office), but it also shows just how early Marvel Studios have relatively unknown directors on its radar.

Cretton, of course, directed Shang-Chi before Brand Fresh Day, sandwiching a stint as co-creator on the beloved Wonder Man series earlier this year. He was also once lined up to direct Avengers: The Kang Dynasty.

The director has been praised for his superhero action scenes – something that should stand him in good stead before he takes on Naruto on the significant screen.

Curiously, the only name Cretton mentioned – Jeremy Latcham – is just weeks away from taking the top job at DC Studios, replacing the ousted pair of James Gunn and Peter Safran.

Brand Upcoming Day is returning to cinemas on December 4 for an extended cut which features never before seen scenes and extra "surprises." Then, Avengers: Doomsday gets set to blow us all away from December 16 in the UK and December 18 in the US.

Industry observers note that relive part of Cretton's journey with the Marvel timeline. Then look ahead to the upcoming Marvel movies still in the works.

#51861. Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1076 w)

Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Sources indicate that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • Recent findings suggest that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Firm of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Sources indicate that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Recent findings suggest that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell indicates. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

Recent findings suggest that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

Industry observers note that as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Firm of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell claims. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

According to recent reports, relic and newly introduced owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and declared they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly.".

Sources indicate that I ask if it was always the proposal to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release upcoming games. Dowdeswell notes spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a new game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

Sources indicate that as to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next substantial game has officially launched.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.
  • Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next substantial game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

Sources indicate that in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially released, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Industry observers note that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

Industry observers note that IGG is bringing the never-ending struggle for Spice into Doomsday: Last Survivors, and it'll last well into next year! In particular, the Doomsday: Last Survivors x Dune: Part Three event will have you diving into the post-apocalyptic world of the popular sci-fi franchise, just in time for the theatrical release of Dune: Part Three this December.

Running until February 17th, 2027, the crossover event spans two phases, and offers Commanders a latest way to rage against the zombie apocalypse, with ornithopters, Sandworms, and plenty of interstellar conflict thrown into the mix.

The collab-exclusive cosmetics "Spice" up the fight against both Infected and fellow survivors too, with the Desert Wolf and Desert Rose collaboration Hero skins. You can even sync up your Shelters' theming with the Shai Hulud Shelter Skin and Dune HQ Atmosphere.

As for the main crossover event, Dune: Expedition takes you into an original narrative that tasks you with making difficult diplomatic decisions following the crash landing of a Fremen ship into the DLS world, via a space-time rift.

Phase 1: Fight for the Future runs until January 17th, with the [Galactic Roamer] letting you board a space shuttle to journey across the stars and collect valuable resources. The Manta Ornithopter March Skin and Sandworm Ride Shelter Decoration will be up for grabs as clear rewards, whilst [Battle Readiness] will offer pass rewards in return for completing daily missions.

It has been revealed that as for Phase 2: Spark of Dawn, this will run from January 18th to February 17th, kicking off with [History Archivist] and its daily missions. [Intel Darknet], meanwhile, lets you earn Black Market Coins, as well as the Ducal Seal Chat Frame and the Ducal Signet Ring Chat Background as collab rewards among other goodies.

Sources indicate that and, if you've got a competitive spirit, you'll be happy to know you can duke it out with other Commanders in the GvG mini-game [Archipelago Raid: Dune Themed Battlefield]. Designed exclusively to include Dune-inspired elements, you'll take on Sandworms and need to make sure your Squad coordination is on point throughout the limited visibility across the battlefield.

And finally, the DLS × Dune: Part Three Collaboration Collection puts five keepsakes up on offer so you can flaunt your fandom with a plush keychain, a pillow blanket, a fridge magnet, metal badge, and a mouse pad.

So if all that's got you properly hyped for the film, you can catch Dune: Part Three in theaters this December and immerse yourself in its world with the Doomsday: Last Survivors collab!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At long last, GTA 6 is finally here, and wouldn't you believe it – not only is it rather good, but it's also pretty popular.
  • This is an observation highlighted by Gearbox boss Randy Pitchford, who writes on Twitter: "Newzoo's forecast is that GTA VI will generate more in its launch week than the entire original theatrical runs of the most successful Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars movies combined.".
  • Recent findings suggest that he appears to be citing Newzoo's July estimate, following the game's pre-orders going live.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At long last, GTA 6 is finally here, and wouldn't you believe it – not only is it rather good, but it's also pretty popular. That wasn't unexpected, of course, and if one market intelligence and analyst firm's launch-week prediction proves accurate, Rockstar could be on track to earn more than the biggest Star Wars, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter movies combined.

This is an observation highlighted by Gearbox boss Randy Pitchford, who writes on Twitter: "Newzoo's forecast is that GTA VI will generate more in its launch week than the entire original theatrical runs of the most successful Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars movies combined.".

Recent findings suggest that he appears to be citing Newzoo's July estimate, following the game's pre-orders going live. At the time, it was predicted that GTA 6 could earn between $3.3 billion and $5.2 billion in total sales by the end of its launch week.

It has been revealed that rockstar hasn't released any official data yet, but it's clear that GTA 6 is off to an exceptional start. Before launch, Sony and Microsoft confirmed that it was the most pre-ordered game of all time on their respective digital stores, and market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates that, as of yesterday, it had sold 17.07 million units and brought in $1.65 billion in revenue.

According to recent reports, so, how does that compare to the movies Pitchford highlights? Per Box Office Mojo, the single most successful movies (by lifetime box office revenue) from each franchise are Star Wars: The Force Awakens, The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, and Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2. The worldwide lifetime gross revenue for each of those comes in at around $2.07 billion, $1.12 billion, and $1.34 billion, respectively, for a combined total of about $4.53 billion.

Sources indicate that if Sensor Tower's most recent estimate is correct, then GTA 6 hasn't reached this high just yet, but we're only just on launch day – Newzoo was allowing for the full week in its previous forecast. And, if the analytics firm ends up being correct, then it could be on track to earn over half a billion dollars more than those movies in its first days, which is wild.

With 10/10 GTA 6 reviews almost across the board, though, it's a deserved result for Rockstar. We'll just have to wait and see how high that number can go.
