📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hunger Games Suzanne Collins doesn't take a backseat to the movies, according to Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence.

Before the latest novel was even published, it was confirmed a film adaptation would also be in the works, telling the prequel story of Haymitch Abernathy – the District 12 victor who went on to mentor Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

In a recent development, "Yeah, she's very involved," Lawrence tells us when we meet with him in London to discuss The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. "When she sends the manuscript, I read it, usually a couple times, and then the first thing we do is we sit in a conference room at the publishing manufacturer that she works through, and we break down the book together. And we've done that since Catching Fire.

Sources indicate that "And then she's on the phone with me and Nina [Jacobson, producer] and the screenwriter every day for hours, probably hundreds of hours of calls talking through the script, and then she kind of disappears when we shoot," he continues. "And then we bring her back in when we have a cut, and she looks at the cut, and we give her the data on tests, and we decide if we have to do any pickups or anything. And then she obviously sees the finished product, so she is very, very involved. She's just not there on the shoot, and part of that is so that she can keep an objective perspective on it for when she sees the cut.".

While the Sunrise on the Reaping film has yet to be released to the public, it's already garnered strongly positive reactions from fans, which kicked off with an outpouring of love for each casting announcement.

In a recent development, "It's wishy-washy with things online, and I feel like, in this day and age, it is a lot easier to be negative, and I feel like the negativity is always a little bit louder," indicates McKenna Grace, who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner. "And so, it's such a blessing whenever you're a part of a fan base, or whenever anything that you're a part of is getting positivity, and for it to be such an overwhelming, kind response, I feel like is just… But it's just been so wonderful that they're happy with it, and that they're accepting us into this franchise.".

Recent findings suggest that joseph Zada, who plays Haymitch, adds: "And even a lot of the people that have been able to see it from press that haven't been fans, or haven't seen the previous films, are just also so excited to see it, which is such a scary thing. [You] walk into a prequel hoping that it can stand alone, and that people that aren't familiar with the franchise can enjoy the film, too.".

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters this November 20. In the meantime, check out our The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review and our guide to all the biggest movie release dates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking over the world tomorrow, World of Warcraft: Forever was the first game this month that people flocked to in record-breaking numbers.

Industry observers note that while we don't know the exact player count like we do with games on Steam, we can make an educated guess on just how many people dove into the MMO via a recent set of statistics from Blizzard. According to the official WoW X account, over 15 million characters were created in the last few weeks.

Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. This is a game where you can put hundreds of hours into one character before ever reaching the level cap. There definitely aren't 15 million total players based on this statistic, but the number might not be massively below that.

I can't say I'm surprised that a spin-off MMO that will remain stuck in the most universally nostalgic era of WoW was a massive hit. Everyone who stopped playing for one reason or another came back to remember what it was like to smack a scorpion for 38 seconds.

In a recent development, whether or not they'll stick around is the question. Blizzard looks on updating the game with new things to do for players at different stages of the long leveling journey. Most people are still weeks away from reaching the level 60 cap, partially because there are so many things to do that don't involve XP. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, UPGRADE 11TH NOVEMBER: Grand Theft Auto 6 has also become the most pre-ordered game "of all time" on the Xbox Store, Microsoft has declared. And on that platform, again, the advice is to pre-load because of "unprecedented demand" for the game, a post on Xbox Wire stated.

The Xbox difference is that you can use Xbox Cloud to stream GTA 6 to other Xbox devices, although not PC, notably - the game isn't available on PC and presumably Rockstar doesn't want it playable there by any means. Microsoft's stream-deal with Rockstar has also expanded to include Red Dead Redemption 2 "and more", which will be available to stream in the "coming months".

ORIGINAL STORY 10TH NOVEMBER: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Industry observers note that last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick mentioned pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

Have you managed to resist pre-ordering it yet?

My mom literally called me to come over to help her water a single outdoor plant, and when I got there she was cooking for my older brother who had been there the entire time.

That wild story is definitely not an outlier either. The angry rants are just pouring out of people, an overwhelming majority of whom are women who feel like they are left doing everything while their siblings live their lives. Some are mad about how they did everything until their parent died, only to find out their absentee sibling(s) got the exact same inheritance. Others are mad about how their family members infrequently show up and then critique the job they were doing and question the decisions they make.

One woman shared that a caretaker in her family was later sued by the surviving family members for taking money out of the disabled parent’s bank account to buy said parent food and medicine. You can check out that banger below, which has about five thousand likes….

With Sister you can also wait for her to spend your dad’s money on essentials for him like groceries or clothes and then sue her later - because she never had financial power of attorney!

Recent findings suggest that seriously, don’t take my word for it. Look wherever the Sister sketch is embedded. You’ll immediately start running into story after story of angry people who need to let it out. I saw one woman calling out the parent they’re looking after for raising her brother to think he didn’t need to help. I’ve seen numerous lawyers, nurses, dementia care workers and doctors saying they see the same dynamic over and over again. I saw one woman say her brother who lives near her mom can’t be bothered to help; so, she has to travel across the country to handle things.

Sources indicate that watching this from my mom’s house 1500 miles away bc my brother Just Can’t Manage to get her to the doctor or the dentist. he lives down the street.

Sources indicate that it’s clear this sketch, which is filled with fun little easter eggs, struck a nerve, but it seems like in a very therapeutic way. It’s allowing people to give voice to frustrations they’ve clearly had for a long time, and if it leads to even some family members doing a little self-reflecting and helping out a bit more, it’ll be a huge victory. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace.
  • As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a latest premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.
  • The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This upcoming feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a latest premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

Sources indicate that for most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis stated that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

In a recent development, interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the firm may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the fresh paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game.
  • Sources indicate that conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more!
  • Recent findings suggest that where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest.

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

Sources indicate that conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Recent findings suggest that where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

While GTA 6 might be literally just around the corner, we've still got a few games launching on Xbox over the next few days, with and today (November 17th) is no exception - although there's literally only two known upcoming releases.

In a recent development, the highlight is Ranger's Path: National Park Simulator, which is an Xbox Play Anywhere title from the publisher behind the likes of Police Simulator: Patrol Officers and Firefighting Simulator: Ignite. It's been on PC since March and has a "Mostly Positive" rating on Steam, but today marks its debut across Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

It's also worth mentioning that we've got two Xbox Game Pass additions today, with PAW Patrol: Dino World arriving for XGP Ultimate and Premium, and Aphelion jumping from Ultimate to Premium for the first time. Neither of these are brand-fresh releases though, so we're not counting them in the list of new Xbox launches.

So, here's what's new on Xbox today (November 17):.

In Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator, you take on the everyday responsibilities of a real park ranger in the stunning Faremont National Park. Restore and maintain scenic trails, assist visitors, and document wildlife in a living, breathing ecosystem.

Step into the magical world of Unicorn Academy and begin your very own adventure! Create your own first-year student at the academy and call upon the help of Unicorn Academy’s favorite characters. Groom, race and bond with your unicorn. Embark on missions to stop Ravenzella’s evil plot.

It has been revealed that ROARR! Sounds like trouble. Did that come from Dino Island? It looks like Rex needs the PAW Patrol to save the day! Mayor Humdinger’s causing chaos. Dinosaurs are scared and running wild. Help them get back to their families safely.

Aphelion is a cinematic third-person action-adventure set on the planet Persephone, an uncharted, frozen world. Stranded and isolated, you must survive the truly unknown, find each other, and complete the mission. Traverse stunning alien landscapes, avoid lurking threats, and discover the haunting secrets buried beneath the ice.

According to recent reports, "With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. Recent findings suggest that modelled after the elven refuge as it appears in Fellowship of the Ring, this kit is a sprawling recreation of the Last Homely House; with over 6,000 pieces to play with, it can create a level of depth and detail most kits can't hope to match. This is the kind of Lego set where you'll discover something new every time you stop to admire it. Lego Rivendell is also impressive enough on display that it'll draw a "woah" worthy of Owen Wilson from most onlookers.

In a recent development, this model often enjoys a price cut in time for the annual Lego Black Friday deals, but this time it's been given an even bigger saving. Actually, it's dropped to an all-time low price that we haven't seen before. Usually, the best we can expect is a reduction down to £365.

Sources indicate that there are four distinct areas for Lego Rivendell; the main house with its tower and display showing off the broken shards of Narsil, the council area with its ring of seats and plinth for the One Ring, a bridge leading to Arwen's pergola, and a woodland smithy where the elves are busy creating masterworks at the forge. Many of these have a mix of exposed and hidden areas you can reveal by lifting off the lid, which really sells the dollhouse-like experience here.

The top half of the tower can be removed to show the room where Bilbo Baggins is staying, for instance, and there's a desk set up where he's writing in his memoirs. (Yes, his minifigure has an alternate face so you can recreate that moment as well - shudder). Meanwhile, Arwen's pergola is removable so that you can get a good look at the forge beneath. Oh, and as for the council area? Well, let's just say Sauron's eye is firmly fixed on this meeting...

Then there are the minifigures. Premium Lego sets like this often come with a lot of figs, but Rivendell feels particularly generous. There are 15 in total; Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin, Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Boromir, Elrond, Arwen, Bilbo, a couple of elves, and a visiting dwarf. That's enough to make the whole kit feel positively alive, and you can recreate a whole host of moments from the movie if you'd like.

It has been revealed that I shouldn't skip over the fact that it's downright beautiful to look at, either. Whether it's the tasteful pastel tiles, the abundance of flora carpeting the grounds, or the autumnal trees looming over it all, Lego Rivendell is an incredibly handsome centerpiece.

It looks like the majority of Lego Lord of the Rings kits are on offer right now; the Balrog Book Nook, Sauron's Helmet, Barad-dur, and Minas Tirith have all been heavily reduced in price at Amazon.

It has been revealed that even with the arrival of Lego Minas Tirith earlier this year (which just got its first discount, by the way), I still don't think Rivendell has been surpassed. Yes, the Gondorian city is jaw-dropping. For one thing, it's very cleverly designed with a forced perspective using multiple scales. For another, it's striking in a way Rivendell isn't; a mass of white walls and towers surround the spur of a mountain, drawing every eye in the room. However (and this is no insult to Minas Tirith - I'm currently in the middle of building it), I still think Rivendell is prettier and has more 'going on' under the surface.

Basically, I'd always point to this kit if someone asked me what I thought the best ever Lego set was - it's captured both my heart and my imagination, just like its inspiration did when I first saw it on-screen in 2001.

In terms of other Lego news, it looks like there will be 10 Lego Star Wars concept art minifigures for the 50th anniversary.

Recent findings suggest that I've been writing about games in one form or another since 2012, but these days you'll find me managing GamesRadar+'s tabletop gaming and toy coverage (I spend my time here handling everything from board game reviews to the latest Lego news). I've also been obsessed with Warhammer since the 1990s, and love nothing more than running tabletop RPGs like D&D as a Dungeon Master.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a initiative laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging fresh video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

Sources indicate that we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is mentioned to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a fresh dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

It's here. GTA 6 has been loosed upon the world, and another nation's productivity goes dark as each advancing hour unleashes midnight unlocks on the next timezone. And hey, from the sounds of it, people seem to like what they're finding—and they're finding a lot.

You can mini-golf. You can go on beach dates. You can text and drive (don't). You can doomscroll, and birdwatch, and ride a jetski with a dog. GTA 6 is dense with possible activities, actions, systems, and mechanics, but not everyone is having the best luck navigating the maelstrom of associated controls and button prompts. Allow me to present Japanese X user @Shunep3_STS, who on this day represents all of us:.

操作が増えて覚えきれず、間違えて２つ買ったシェイクをしゃがみ歩きしながら飲み干すヤバい奴になってる https://t.co/OLXaEQGc7CNovember 18, 2026.

"There are so many fresh controls I can’t keep them all straight," remarked @Shunep3_STS via machine translation, "and now I’m that guy chugging two shakes I accidentally bought while walking around in a squat.".

It has been revealed that there's something magical about this image. To begin with, the scene—like all of GTA 6—looks profoundly, almost grotesquely expensive: the delicate feathering of Jason's forearm hair, the pseudo-memoji of Cal in the text message notification, the fidelity of pebbled sand that probably cost more to realize in-game than I've spent on rent in the last three years. It's a tableau of technological excess.

And all of that's being deployed to present a man double-fisting slushies in an empty parking lot as he skulks like an imperiled raccoon. Look at him! Look at his face! He's got his chiseled jaw set like he's Solid Snake, but he's nursing a tummy full of iced corn syrup because the pilot controlling his body got too overwhelmed by which buttons do what.

Industry observers note that and he's not alone: Our own Andrea Shearon is one of the many struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of button prompts in GTA 6. "There's so much going on," she said. "I just walk up to people and kind of mash all the face buttons for a surprise. You never know if I'm gonna punch someone or do squats or flip them off.".

She's spent a lot of time accidentally making rude gestures at her snake as a result.

We're all, at some point, a man huddling in the dark, trying to figure out how to put down his sippy cups.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The fresh season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each upcoming season.

It has been revealed that you’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The fresh season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Sources indicate that blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

Industry observers note that in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to a upcoming Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest.
  • "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff.

According to a upcoming Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.

"Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore upcoming creative opportunities".

Fairgames was initially declared in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue.

Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely. Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December.

The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026, following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond.

Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles, Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release.

Recent findings suggest that throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May, but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S officially celebrated their sixth anniversaries back on November 10th, and to mark the occasion, Niko Partners analyst Daniel Ahmad has been looking into a whole bunch of sales estimates.

In a post over on social media, Ahmad estimated that the Series X and S are now at a combined 38 million sales worldwide, and then compared that figure to loads of other consoles that we've seen throughout the years.

The comparison is specifically referencing the sales of each console after six years on the market, so when the Xbox 360 is referenced at 60 million sales, for example, it still racked up another 20+ million until it was discontinued.

In a recent development, as you can see, it doesn't make for great reading overall. Sony has shipped a lot more PS5 consoles than Microsoft has Xbox consoles throughout this generation, and even compared to past Xbox systems, the Series X and S have struggled to keep pace. That remarked, the original Xbox only racked up around 25m sales, so that one's been beaten at least.

Ahmad also points out that "console players are monetizing at levels significantly higher than any prior gen", so even though hardware sales have been poor for Xbox, content and services revenue has grown massively in recent years.

Sources indicate that people will point to this kind of stuff as evidence that Xbox is "failing", but Microsoft is much more interested in the content and services side of things, and that's been a much bigger success for them since the Xbox Series X and S first launched. With Project Helix around the corner though, they'll still hope they can attract a bigger piece of the pie in the hardware space, although that'll be a very tough ask amidst an ongoing component crisis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next significant update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Sources indicate that previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive tech giant’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Fresh Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

Sources indicate that the first latest Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

It has been revealed that the second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

Industry observers note that the higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

It has been revealed that re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this enhancement is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

According to recent reports, when an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a fresh Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.
